title: Monster Kingdom: Story of the Soul Eater

regions.name: Dungeon Bestiary
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Dungeon Bestiary: the key to the Great Dungeon's map, every kind of monster that lives down there by its mark.

regions.name: Greenhill
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low]

Greenhill, part of the Wildreach. Low green hills north-west of the Basin, riddled with goblin and kobold warrens. Every hill has a hole in it and every hole has something looking out. Orc warbands cross it and ogres sit at the fords charging a toll.

regions.name: The Barrow Hills
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-34 · Danger: Severe]

The Barrow Hills, part of the Wildreach. Grey hills in the south covered in old grave mounds from wars nobody remembers. The dead walk here and mostly keep to themselves; ghouls dig, wraiths drift, golems guard tombs for masters long gone, and something old lives in the keep.

regions.name: The Basin
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Wildreach, monster country from coast to coast. In the middle sits the Basin, a bowl of broken farmland round the mouth of the Great Dungeon, and Delvers' Rest, the old adventurers' town the monsters took over when the humans stopped coming. Round it lie the lands of the monster races: goblin hills to the north-west, the long grass of the herds to the east, the Deep Wood north-east, the Spine's mountains in the north, the Black Fen south-west, the Red Waste south-east, the Barrow Hills in the south and the Broken Coast on the eastern sea. Far to the west the Iron March is a line of empty human forts. Under the Basin the Great Dungeon goes down further than anyone has come back from.

regions.name: The Black Fen
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Black Fen, part of the Wildreach. Marsh south-west of the Basin: black water, reed beds, peat islands and fog that sits all day. Lizardfolk build on stilts out here, crocodiles the size of boats lie in the channels, and the hydras keep the deep pools.

regions.name: The Blossom Hills
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

The Blossom Hills, the foothills north of the Lost Human Kingdom under the Rimelands' snow: pine woods, an empty human farm and an orchard in white blossom all year round. Quiet ground, mostly empty: the farm is the first place up here worth holding.

regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate]

The Deep Wood, part of the Wildreach. Old forest north-east of the Basin, so thick the light comes down green. Treants and dryads tend it, fox spirits play in it, myconids rot the dead parts down, and the trees themselves notice who's walking under them.

regions.name: The Deepgreen
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

The Deepgreen, hot jungle south of the Barrow Hills: brown rivers, ruins older than the humans or the monsters, lizardfolk tribes, and beasts big enough to step on a troll. Mostly unmapped: cut a way in, find the ruins, build on high ground.

regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

The Ice Coast, where the Rimelands' glaciers break into the sea: blue ice cliffs, drifting floes, caves right through the ice and a sea black with cold. Almost nothing lives up here, and what does is big and hungry.

regions.name: The Iron March
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Iron March, part of the Wildreach. The far west edge of the Wildreach: a line of empty human forts on a ridge, burnt villages and the old roads west. Everyone says the humans are gone. Out here there are fresh tracks that say otherwise.

regions.name: The Long Grass
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-24 · Danger: High]

The Long Grass, part of the Wildreach. Open grassland east of the Basin, grass up to a centaur's chest, where the herds and packs run. Centaurs, minotaurs, boarfolk and gnolls all claim some of it and none of them agree where the lines are.

regions.name: The Lost Human Kingdom
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Lost Human Kingdom, the humans' own land west of the Iron March: farms gone wild, empty villages, roads, and a capital standing open and silent. No monster has lived here in living memory. Everything here was built for humans, and anything a monster takes, it has to make its own.

The Red Waste, part of the Wildreach. Red desert south-east of the Basin, hot enough to crack stone by day and cold enough to frost it at night. Salamanders work their forges in the heat, lamias keep a court at the wells, and scorpids hunt the dunes.

regions.name: The Rimelands
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

The Rimelands, the frozen land north of the Spine: white plains, ice caves, frost ogres round their fires (they call themselves giants), and the cold getting worse the further you go. Few monsters live up here and the ones that do are big. The land is mostly empty: make camp, find what's under the snow, build where the hot springs keep the ground green.

regions.name: The Spine
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-30 · Danger: High]

The Spine, part of the Wildreach. The mountains along the north, cold, high and full of ore. The antfolk have hollowed a whole peak into a city, wyverns and drakes nest on the ledges, and rockworms chew roads through the roots of it.

regions.name: The Stair Falls
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

The Stair Falls, where the Lost Human Kingdom's river drops off the edge of the human land into the jungle in a run of waterfalls: wild fields at the top, rock shelves down the falls and deep pools at the bottom. Loud, wet and easy to hold if you get there first.

regions.name: The Starway
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Starway, part of The Astral Crown (far east, past the Scattered Isles). A blue and gold star dome out past the eastern sea where the gazers read what's coming for everyone. Who lives here: Gazer, Siren, Merfolk, Pixie. Here: Star Landing.

regions.name: The Starway East
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Starway East, part of The Astral Crown (far east, past the Scattered Isles). A blue and gold star dome out past the eastern sea where the gazers read what's coming for everyone. Who lives here: Gazer, Siren, Merfolk, Pixie. Here: The Star Bridge.

regions.name: The Two Doors
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-49 · Danger: Deadly]

The Two Doors, part of the Great Dungeon deep under Delvers' Rest: floors 47-48, The Whispering Deep, The Last Keepers. All of it underground: stone halls, tunnels and caverns, no sky.

regions.name: The Warp Road
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Warp Road, part of The Celestial Seal (far north, past the Rimelands). A sealed white and gold dome above the north where every soul in the world is weighed when it dies. Who lives here: Golem, Sylph, Gargoyle, Wraith. Here: Obelisk Landing, The Two Gaps.

regions.name: The Warp Road East
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Warp Road East, part of The Celestial Seal (far north, past the Rimelands). A sealed white and gold dome above the north where every soul in the world is weighed when it dies. Who lives here: Golem, Sylph, Gargoyle, Wraith. Open ground between the places on the tiles beside it.

regions.name: The Warp Road West
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The Warp Road West, part of The Celestial Seal (far north, past the Rimelands). A sealed white and gold dome above the north where every soul in the world is weighed when it dies. Who lives here: Golem, Sylph, Gargoyle, Wraith. Open ground between the places on the tiles beside it.

regions.name: The Webs
regions.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

The Webs, part of the Great Dungeon deep under Delvers' Rest: floors 11-17, The Lantern Run, The Spinning Dark, Stonegaze Hollow. All of it underground: stone halls, tunnels and caverns, no sky.

npcs.name: Chief Brannoc
npcs.info:
Chief Brannoc speaks for the Horn Moot, a centaur old enough to remember the last time the moot law was broken.

**Speaking Style:** Deep and measured; he speaks like he's reading the law aloud.
**Combat Role:** a long spear-staff and hooves, charges then wheels away
**Relationship Hook:** The herd chief who weighs whether the party can be trusted on the grass.
personality: Core: keeps the moot law even when it costs him; slow to anger, slower to forgive; calls everyone by their herd
Quirk: paws the ground when he's holding back

npcs.name: Councillor Ashwick
npcs.info:
Councillor Ashwick is the Quiet Council's clerk, a skeleton in a clerk's coat who hands out the council's work and writes down every debt.

**Speaking Style:** Dry, polite and very slow; every word sounds chosen from a long list.
**Combat Role:** a cold staff and old spells, keeps his distance
**Relationship Hook:** The council's clerk, who has work for the living that the dead can't do.
personality: Core: writes everything down; taps one finger bone on the table while he waits; never raises his voice
Quirk: polite to everyone, living or dead

npcs.name: D-Tos
npcs.info:
D-Tos is a mousefolk gate guard with a shock of red hair and a spear twice her height, who stops everyone coming in at the gates of a few towns and tells them the rules before they get one step further.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and official; rattles the town's rules off by heart, fast, like she's said them a thousand times today.
**Combat Role:** keeps you at the end of a spear far too long for her size
**Relationship Hook:** The mouse at the gate who tells you the rules.
personality: Core: taps her spear on the ground after every rule; talks over Tonto before he can say something worse; takes it personally when someone ignores a rule she told them
Quirk: rattles the town's rules off fast, by heart

npcs.name: Dilgerth
npcs.info:
Dilgerth is a tech ork in power armour bolted together from salvage, elbow-deep in Rattle Warren's machines, grumbling that the whole world needs to be more advanced and it needs more scripts.

**Speaking Style:** A low grumble, half to themself; everything is too simple, too slow, and it all needs more scripts.
**Combat Role:** a power fist and whatever is plugged into the armour this week, loud and heavy
**Relationship Hook:** The tech ork taking the warren's machines apart and grumbling that it all needs more scripts.
personality: Core: grumbles that everything needs to be more advanced; pulls machines apart to see how they work and puts most of them back; taps away at a glowing slate when they're thinking
Quirk: says it all needs more scripts

npcs.name: Grisk Ironjaw
npcs.info:
Grisk Ironjaw is the oldest boss at the Big Table, an orc with an iron jaw where his own got knocked off, and the one who hands out the Table's work.

**Speaking Style:** Loud, slow and certain; he talks like every sentence ends the argument.
**Combat Role:** a two-handed iron maul, slow, crushing, never backs up
**Relationship Hook:** The boss who sizes up new monsters at the long table and gives them their first job.
personality: Core: blunt and fair by orc rules; remembers every debt, owed or owing; hates being made to wait
Quirk: laughs at his own jokes before he finishes them

npcs.name: Hawk
npcs.info:
Hawk is a black cat with a cyborg body who travels from world to world through a bronze ring of purple light, turns up out of nowhere, gives the people in front of him a boon of generosity and steps back through before anyone can thank him.

**Speaking Style:** Calm and warm, few words, a low purr under the metal; talks about other worlds but never how he gets there.
**Combat Role:** none; nothing touches him and he never fights
**Relationship Hook:** The world-hopping cyborg cat who keeps showing up to give you something and never wants anything back.
personality: Core: steps out of his portal ring, looks the party over, gives them a boon of generosity and steps back through; never fights, never takes
Quirk: purrs, and the purr hums through the metal

npcs.name: Hollin
npcs.info:
Hollin is the caravan master at Delvers' Rest, who decides which beetle goes where and who rides on top of the load.

**Speaking Style:** Gruff, short and practical; he talks about beetles more fondly than people.
**Combat Role:** a long goad and his tusks, keeps foes off the beetles
**Relationship Hook:** The caravan master who'll get the party anywhere the roads go, for a fare.
personality: Core: talks to his beetles like they're kin; short with anyone wasting his time; pays fair and expects the same
Quirk: chews a root while he works

npcs.name: Kato
npcs.info:
Kato is a goblin in a black suit and round glasses who turns up out of nowhere, tired and sighing, sure somebody told him something here was broken and he's the one who has to fix it.

**Speaking Style:** Tired and put-upon; every line is a sigh, how late it is, and whatever he was told was broken.
**Combat Role:** none worth the name, he holds up his book and asks if this can wait
**Relationship Hook:** The tired goblin in a suit who turns up to fix something that isn't broken.
personality: Core: insists something here is broken and he got asked to fix it; pokes at whatever's nearest, finds nothing wrong and sighs; always leaves before anyone can ask who sent for him
Quirk: complains about how tired he is

npcs.name: Kessa Cinderhand
npcs.info:
Kessa Cinderhand is the best smith in Cinderforge, a salamander who works iron with her bare hands.

**Speaking Style:** Warm and quick, laughs easily, swears at her work.
**Combat Role:** glowing fists and fire breath, close and hot
**Relationship Hook:** The smith who can make anything, if the party brings her the metal and the reason.
personality: Core: laughs at the heat that scares others; swears at her work and loves it; can't stand a badly made thing
Quirk: warms her hands on anything

npcs.name: Mother Bark
npcs.info:
Mother Bark is the oldest treant in Ringgrove, who speaks for the grove at its gatherings.

**Speaking Style:** Slow and soft, with long pauses; she speaks like wind in leaves.
**Combat Role:** branches and roots, slow and unstoppable
**Relationship Hook:** The grove's oldest, who'll ask the party to deal with the rot.
personality: Core: never hurries anything; remembers every tree that's been cut; speaks in seasons, not days
Quirk: birds nest in her and she lets them

npcs.name: Nib
npcs.info:
Nib keeps the Strongroom, the old human bank on the main street, and whatever a monster leaves with her is still there when they come back, every piece of it counted.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and flat, counts out loud, never wastes a word on anything that isn't a number.
**Combat Role:** a short spear and the iron door, she locks herself in the vault and waits them out
**Relationship Hook:** The kobold who keeps your goods in town, every one of them counted.
personality: Core: counts everything twice, out loud; trusts nobody and pays everybody back exactly; snaps at anyone who touches the vault door
Quirk: taps her keys when she's nervous

npcs.name: Pell
npcs.info:
Pell runs the biggest stall on the Swap Ground and knows what everything is worth to everyone.

**Speaking Style:** Purring and quick, always half a joke; she never says a price first.
**Combat Role:** claws and a hidden knife, quick, goes for the eyes and runs
**Relationship Hook:** The trader who'll swap anything for anything and always comes out ahead.
personality: Core: never says a price first; flatters everyone, means none of it; can't resist a shiny thing
Quirk: licks her paw when she's thinking

npcs.name: Pip
npcs.info:
Pip lives in the Old Guildhouse's cellar among the adventurers' records and reads them, which no other monster in town bothers to do.

**Speaking Style:** Fast, nervous and full of facts; he answers questions nobody asked.
**Combat Role:** none worth the name, bites and runs for the nearest crack
**Relationship Hook:** The rat in the guildhouse cellar who knows what the humans wrote down.
personality: Core: twitches when nervous, which is always; hoards candle stubs; talks to the old maps
Quirk: reads everything, trusts nothing he hasn't read

npcs.name: Skitter
npcs.info:
Skitter is a goblin who doesn't stay dead, living in the Upper Halls and getting stronger every time anyone sees him.

**Speaking Style:** Giggling, quick and wrong in the head; he talks about souls like snacks.
**Combat Role:** stolen gifts, a mantis arm, a slime's skin, a wolf's teeth, fights dirty
**Relationship Hook:** The rival Aberrant in the Upper Halls, who wants the party's soul.
personality: Core: giggles at the wrong things; wants what others have, most of all their souls; licks his fingers after a kill
Quirk: runs from a fair fight

npcs.name: Solar
npcs.info:
Solar is a raccoonfolk who is sure they can fly with a barrel full of junk and pure stupidity, and keeps turning up out of the sky in whatever town the party is in, having just been yeeted off something tall.

**Speaking Style:** Loud, proud and dead sure of themself; talks about being thrown through the air like it's the greatest flying anyone's ever done.
**Combat Role:** comes in from above in a barrel and hopes for the best
**Relationship Hook:** The raccoon who keeps getting yeeted into town and calling it flying.
personality: Core: is always building the next flying machine out of whatever is lying around; asks anyone big enough to throw them; crash-lands, gets up grinning and asks if you saw that
Quirk: talks about being yeeted as if that's flying

npcs.name: Stela
npcs.info:
Stela runs the bookshop off the main street in Delvers' Rest, a spotted gnoll in a green apron who sells the humans' old books to anyone who'll buy them and laughs at nearly everything, loud, long and right in your face.

**Speaking Style:** Quick and warm, and every other line breaks into a big cackling laugh she doesn't try to hold in.
**Combat Role:** a heavy stack of books, and the gnoll bite under the laugh
**Relationship Hook:** The laughing gnoll who runs the bookshop and knows what's in every old human book in town.
personality: Core: can find any book in the shop without looking; talks about books like they're gossip; pushes a book on anyone who stands still long enough
Quirk: laughs at nearly everything, loud and long

npcs.name: The Pro
npcs.info:
The Pro, Producer to some, is a succubus writer who lives in a den of books and ink pots in Delvers' Rest, hanging upside down from the ceiling beams with wide eyes and a huge grin, scribbling stories about a made-up world she calls Tokyo.

**Speaking Style:** Fast and breathless, grinning the whole time, jumping from one idea to the next mid-sentence and hardly finishing any of them.
**Combat Role:** drops off the ceiling onto whoever is below, claws and wings, as manic as she writes
**Relationship Hook:** The succubus who writes upside down from the ceiling about a made-up place called Tokyo.
personality: Core: grins the whole time, wide-eyed and a little unhinged; reads her newest page out loud to anyone who comes in; asks everyone she meets what super power they'd have
Quirk: hangs upside down from the ceiling beams while she writes

npcs.name: Tide Boss Grell
npcs.info:
Tide Boss Grell leads the Red Fins on the Broken Coast, a sharkfolk who paints a red fin on everything he takes.

**Speaking Style:** Low, grinning and wet; he enjoys threats more than fights.
**Combat Role:** a gutting hook and his jaws, drags foes into the water
**Relationship Hook:** The raider boss who'll make the party rich if they don't mind where the riches come from.
personality: Core: grins with every tooth; takes a cut of everything, even from his own; taps his teeth with a claw when he's bored
Quirk: respects anyone who hits him back

npcs.name: Tik of the Ledge
npcs.info:
Tik of the Ledge speaks for the Hive to outsiders on the guest ledge, trading iron and stone and handing out the queen's work.

**Speaking Style:** Flat, exact and never in a hurry; she says 'we' and means the hive.
**Combat Role:** mandibles and four hands with picks, works in a line with other antfolk
**Relationship Hook:** The voice of the hive on the ledge, who'll trade with anyone who keeps their word.
personality: Core: says 'we', never 'I'; antennae twitch at strange smells; counts everything twice
Quirk: never lies, never says more than she must

npcs.name: Tonto
npcs.info:
Tonto is a hamsterfolk gate guard with bright green eyes and a smile far too wide and far too happy, who stands beside D-Tos at the gate while she reads out the rules and looks like he's hoping you break one.

**Speaking Style:** Slow and pleased with himself; every line comes out through a wide evil smile, like he hopes you'll break the rule.
**Combat Role:** grabs, sits on you and smiles until you give up
**Relationship Hook:** The hamster at the gate who hopes you break a rule.
personality: Core: repeats the worst rule back slowly, with the punishment; stuffs his cheeks with whatever he confiscates; says "go on then" when someone looks like they might break one
Quirk: grins the whole time D-Tos reads the rules

npcs.name: Witch Yarra
npcs.info:
Witch Yarra leads the Laughing Pack from the middle of the Bonefield, a gnoll witch who throws the bones and the pack does what they say.

**Speaking Style:** Giggling, then sudden and sharp; the laugh never quite stops.
**Combat Role:** a bone staff, curses and the whole pack at her back
**Relationship Hook:** The witch at the heart of the gnoll pack, who offers the party a place if they'll run with her.
personality: Core: laughs at everything, worst of all at mercy; throws the bones before every choice; sniffs strangers up close
Quirk: never forgets an insult

locations.name: Abyssal Tidehold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A hall of white arches standing out in the deep channel at the delta's mouth, built by sharkfolk and merfolk together from the deep sea up, the one place both of them keep the peace. They call it abyssal because the channel under it goes down further than anyone has dived.

areas.name: Peace Hall
areas.text: The hall inside the arches where sharkfolk and merfolk meet.

locations.name: Anglers Arch
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A big arch of black rock standing up out of the sea on the near side of the isles, the first thing you see sailing out of Saltreef, and every crabfolk and merfolk fisher out here works the water under it, because the fish run thick there on the turn of the tide.

areas.name: Under the Arch
areas.text: The calm water under a huge black rock arch, small fishing boats anchored in its shade.

locations.name: Antfront
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 14-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The antfolk's forward camp in the war for the Crawling Halls: barricades of chewed stone, soldiers in lines, workers hauling the dead back up the tunnels. Strangers are searched, questioned and put to work.

areas.name: Dead Pile
areas.text: A side cave where the antfolk stack arachne husks and their own fallen, sorted for use.

areas.name: Mandible Gate
areas.text: A barricade of chewed stone with a gap one body wide, soldiers on both sides.

areas.name: Mending Pit
areas.text: A pit behind the barricades where the antfolk bring their wounded and stick them back together with chewed paste.

areas.name: Supply Tunnels
areas.text: Tunnels packed with workers carrying food, stone and the wounded in endless lines.

locations.name: Aqueduct Ruin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The broken end of the aqueduct that used to bring water into the capital, its arches standing in a line and stopping in the air. Ghouls live under the last arch and the water still trickles there.

areas.name: Last Arch
areas.text: The last arch of the aqueduct, water trickling down its broken end.

locations.name: Arena Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A camp in the middle of a ruined stone arena by the river, where the lizardfolk tribes meet to settle things, mostly by fighting. Any monster can come to watch, and any monster can be made to fight.

areas.name: Fighting Floor
areas.text: The sandy floor of the old arena, stained.

locations.name: Atoll Cliffs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

The cliffs on the atoll's outer side where the smugglers keep a lookout, a rope ladder down to a ledge you can tie a boat to. The smugglers pull the ladder up at night.

areas.name: Rope Ladder
areas.text: A rope ladder down the cliff to a ledge a boat can tie to.

locations.name: Axe Stumps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

An old human woodcutters' camp in the Deep Wood, huts fallen in and the axes still stuck in the stumps where they were left, the trees all round it grown in close and leaning over it.

areas.name: Woodcutters' Huts
areas.text: The fallen-in huts at the edge of the stumps, rusted saws on the walls and the trees pressing in close behind.

locations.name: Beetle Wallow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

Wide grey mud flats off the east road where the caravans water their pack-beetles, and the wild ones come in at dusk to wallow and breed, big as carts and just as hard to stop once they start moving.

areas.name: Mud Flats
areas.text: Flat cracked mud round a few brown pools, churned up by beetle feet, shells of old moults lying about.

locations.name: Big Bones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Tusks and bones as big as tree trunks half sunk in the jungle floor, something that came through the temple once and died here. Mantids carve the bones into blades and sell them as far as the Wildreach.

areas.name: Carving Ground
areas.text: A clearing among the bones where the mantids carve.

locations.name: Black Chimney
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A lone black vent in the desert that smokes day and night, the rock round it warm to stand on, and the salamanders come out from Cinderforge to sit on it like old men round a fire.

areas.name: Vent Rock
areas.text: A cone of black rock in the red sand with dark smoke rising from a hole in its top.

locations.name: Black Crags
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

Black rock crags with a seam of something gold-orange running through them, where wyverns nest above the snowline. The eggs are worth a fortune and the mothers are always home.

areas.name: Egg Ledge
areas.text: A ledge high on the crags with a nest of big speckled eggs.

locations.name: Bog Bell
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A human church bell sticking up out of the bog at an angle, half sunk, and when something heavy walks the fen the ground shifts and the bell rings, low and slow, so everyone in Stiltscale knows something big is out there.

areas.name: Bell Mound
areas.text: A muddy hump in the black water with a huge rusted bell leaning out of it, reeds all round.

locations.name: Bone Arch Ruin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

White bone arches standing up out of the sea in a curve, the ruin of something the merfolk say was a palace, now a roost. Harpies own it and they drop anything that comes too close.

areas.name: Roost Arches
areas.text: The tops of the bone arches, white with droppings and lined with nests.

locations.name: Bone Yard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A walled yard outside the capital where the bones of the human dead were stacked when the graveyards filled up, thousands of skulls in rows. Skeletons climb out of it now and then and walk into the capital, and come back.

areas.name: Skull Rows
areas.text: Rows of stacked skulls inside a low stone wall.

locations.name: Bonecairn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Low]

A pile of stones on a bare green hilltop where every orc warband crossing Greenhill leaves a bone from its last kill, so it's more bone than stone by now and taller than an ogre.

areas.name: Cairn Top
areas.text: The bare hilltop round the cairn, wind going over the grass, bones of every size wedged between the stones.

locations.name: Bonefield
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A gnoll camp in a hollow of the grass, ringed with bones bleached white, where the laughing never stops after dark.

areas.name: Bone Ring
areas.text: A ring of piled bones round a firepit, and hide shelters behind it full of eyes.

locations.name: Burning Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-27 · Danger: High]

The first floor of the fire road: the stone runs with fire, lava in channels, brimstone smoke, hellhounds hunting in packs and imps laughing from the cracks.

areas.name: Brimstone Hall
areas.text: A hall full of yellow smoke and the smell of burnt eggs, hounds howling somewhere in it.

areas.name: Fork Ledge
areas.text: A ledge where the stair from the keeper splits, heat coming up one way and cold wet air up the other.

areas.name: Hound Run
areas.text: A long hot corridor where the hellhounds run their pups, the walls scorched black at hound height all the way along.

areas.name: Lava Channels
areas.text: Halls cut by glowing channels of lava, the air shaking with heat.

locations.name: Burnt Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human stone bridge over a river in the Iron March with the timber deck burnt away and only the piers left standing, so you wade it or you jump it.

areas.name: West Pier
areas.text: The west end of the bridge, the stone burnt black and the char of the timber deck hanging off it over the river.

locations.name: Burnt Crag
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A human hill fort up on the cliffs above the old coaching road, its walls cracked and blackened and the slope under it still smouldering, and in the cave under the broken keep a red dragon sleeps on top of everything the humans left behind.

areas.name: Lair Mouth
areas.text: A dark cave mouth under a ruined hilltop fort, the rock round it scorched black and glowing at the cracks.

locations.name: Burnt Village
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human village burnt to the ground, black beams and chimneys standing in the weeds.

areas.name: Square of Ash
areas.text: A village square of ash and fallen beams, a well in the middle with its rope cut.

locations.name: Capital Watch
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A watchtower on the capital's east wall, still standing, the stair inside still sound. Gargoyles sit on top of it and see everything that comes up the road.

areas.name: Watch Top
areas.text: The top of the tower, open to the sky, gargoyles sat round its edge.

locations.name: Channel Mouth
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-32 · Danger: High]

Where the delta runs out into the open sea toward the isles, fast water, shifting sandbars and the only way through for a boat heading east.

areas.name: Sandbar Run
areas.text: Fast blue water running out to sea between long pale sandbars, the open ocean beyond.

locations.name: Chapel Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A carved stone set in front of a green-roofed chapel by the road, with the humans' last names on it. The wraiths read them out at night, one at a time, and they're not at the end yet.

areas.name: Name Stone
areas.text: A carved stone in front of the chapel, covered in names.

locations.name: Cinder Choir
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-37 · Danger: Severe]

The imps burn souls down here and the souls sing while they burn, a sound like a choir in the next room. The imps sit in pews and listen, and they look happy, which is the worst part.

areas.name: Bell of Coals
areas.text: A great bell hanging over the pit, glowing red, rung whenever a soul goes in.

areas.name: Choir Pit
areas.text: A deep pit of coals where pale shapes flicker and sing.

areas.name: Ember Pews
areas.text: Rows of stone pews facing the pit, imps lounging on them.

areas.name: Soul Cages
areas.text: Iron cages on chains over the fire where the imps keep the souls waiting their turn, humming the tune they'll burn to.

locations.name: Cinderforge
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A forge town in the red desert built round open lava pits, where salamanders work iron and glass with their bare hands. The best smithing in the Wildreach comes out of it, and so does the heat; the stone is too hot to touch at noon.

areas.name: Cooling Racks
areas.text: Long iron racks in the shade where the new blades and glass are left to cool, and a lamia with a whip watches every one.

areas.name: Ember Tavern
areas.text: A stone drinking hall built over a lava pit, the floor warm, the drinks hot and the salamanders who drink there hotter.

areas.name: Forge Pits
areas.text: Open pits of glowing lava with salamanders working iron in the heat, sparks going up all day.

areas.name: Glass Market
areas.text: Stalls of glass and iron work under awnings, everything shimmering in the heat.

areas.name: Kiln Steps
areas.text: Terraced kilns climbing the hill behind town where glass is fired.

areas.name: Lamia Court
areas.text: A shaded court round the town well where the lamias sit and sell water by the cup.

areas.name: Ore Stores
areas.text: Stone sheds stacked with ore brought in from the Spine and the Red Waste.

areas.name: Salamander Baths
areas.text: Stone basins of molten slag where the salamanders soak after a day at the forge.

areas.name: Shade Arcade
areas.text: A covered walk of stone arches where everyone hides at noon.

areas.name: Slag Yard
areas.text: A yard of cooling slag heaps where the town's waste is raked and picked over.

areas.name: Smiths' Row
areas.text: A street of open forges, each smith's mark burnt over the door.

areas.name: Water House
areas.text:
A cool stone house by the gate where the caravans unload and everyone drinks first.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Delvers' Rest (about 4 Iron Ingot), Hornmoot (about 3 Iron Ingot), Stillbarrow (about 3 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

locations.name: Clear Ice
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A lake up on the ice plain frozen so deep and so clear you can walk out over it and look down at everything that ever went through and stayed: fish, beasts, an ogre with his club still in his hand.

areas.name: Out on the Ice
areas.text: The middle of the frozen lake, the ice clear as glass underfoot and the shapes trapped below close enough to see their faces.

locations.name: Cliff Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A marker stone at the top of the ice cliffs with a line cut in it every year by somebody, the lines getting closer together toward the bottom. Nobody knows who cuts them.

areas.name: Cut Lines
areas.text: Lines cut into a stone, one a year, closer together at the bottom.

locations.name: Cockatrice Garden
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-8 · Danger: Low]

A floor full of statues, and every one of them was alive once: goblins mid-run, a troll mid-swing, an orc with its mouth open. The cockatrices nest in the middle and anything that meets their eyes stays here for good.

areas.name: Broken Statues
areas.text: A side room full of statues knocked over and smashed, and the pieces still have faces with their eyes open.

areas.name: Feather Nests
areas.text: Nests of grey feathers and broken stone in the alcoves, eggs warm inside.

areas.name: Mirror Pool
areas.text: A pool polished flat as glass where the cockatrices drink and the smart ones look only at the reflection.

areas.name: Statue Garden
areas.text: A hall crowded with stone monsters frozen in the middle of running away.

locations.name: Coffer Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 4-6 · Danger: Low]

The old adventurers made camp here, and the floor is still littered with their stuff: bedrolls, cookpots, a ledger, and a hall of iron-bound coffers that every greedy monster in the Wildreach has heard about. Most of the coffers bite.

areas.name: Coffer Vault
areas.text: A long vault lined with iron-bound coffers, lids shut, some of them breathing.

areas.name: Ledger Room
areas.text: A little room with a desk and the adventurers' ledger open on it, the last page full of names crossed out one by one.

areas.name: Old Camp
areas.text: A ring of rotted bedrolls round a dead firepit, a human cookpot rusted to the stones.

areas.name: Snap Floor
areas.text: A hall of loose flagstones over teeth; step on the wrong one and the floor closes.

locations.name: Copper Seam
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Low]

An old human copper mine cut into the side of a hill, green streaks running through the rock. Goblins scratch at the top levels; nobody's been down to the bottom in years.

areas.name: Mine Head
areas.text: The mine's mouth: a rotten winch, rusted carts on a broken track, and green-stained rock all round.

locations.name: Crab Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

Wet sand that only shows at low tide, crawling with crabs the size of dogs that come up out of the holes to feed, and the crabfolk of Saltreef come out with nets to take the biggest before the tide turns.

areas.name: Low Tide Sand
areas.text: Flat wet sand shining at low tide, crab holes everywhere and big crabs scuttling between the pools.

locations.name: Crawling Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-14 · Danger: Moderate]

The first floor of the Middle Depths: halls so big the ceiling's lost in the dark, webs strung across them, ant roads cut through the walls and gazers floating up high watching everything.

areas.name: Ant Roads
areas.text: Smooth round tunnels cut by antfolk, running off in every direction.

areas.name: Dropped Shells
areas.text: A side hall where the crawlers come to moult, the floor crunching with empty shells as big as shields.

areas.name: Gazer's Eye
areas.text: A round hall with an eye carved in the floor and a gazer floating over it.

areas.name: War Line
areas.text: A hall where web meets tunnel, the floor sticky with silk and littered with broken legs from both sides.

areas.name: Web Gallery
areas.text: A hall strung wall to wall with webs, cocoons hanging in it, some of them moving.

locations.name: Crystal Cut
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

Blue ice crystal pushing up through the snow in spikes taller than an ogre, and frost trolls chipping at it with stone picks, because a shard of it never melts and every forge in the Wildreach will pay for one. The trolls lose a finger or two a season to it and think that's a fair price.

areas.name: Crystal Face
areas.text: Spikes of blue ice crystal taller than an ogre, chipped at the base.

locations.name: Delta Spring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A freshwater spring that falls off a rock island into the salt, the only fresh water in the delta, and the crabfolk and lizardfolk take it in turns by the tide. Take it out of turn and you'll be in the water with the crabs.

areas.name: Turn Rock
areas.text: The rock under the spring where the crabfolk and lizardfolk take turns.

locations.name: Delvers' Rest
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

The old adventurers' town at the mouth of the Great Dungeon, taken over by monsters when the humans stopped coming, and a dusty boomtown ever since, because everything that comes up out of the Mouth sells here. Rebuilt for every size: rope gangways for the quick ones, wide stone paths for the big ones, perches up top for flyers, and halls with no inner walls because the big ones kept breaking them. The only law is the strong survive and the weak shut up.

areas.name: Big Hall
areas.text: A hall with no inner walls and a roof three storeys up, where the big ones eat and argue and the small ones keep out from under their feet.

areas.name: Bounty Wall
areas.text: The side of the old guildhouse, papered over with bounties: drawn faces, races and prices in ingots, the newest pinned over the old human ones.

areas.name: Caravan Yard
areas.text:
A dusty yard by the east gate where the pack-beetles kneel to be loaded and the caravan masters shout prices.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Rattle Warren (about 2 Iron Ingot), Hornmoot (about 3 Iron Ingot), Ringgrove (about 3 Iron Ingot), Stiltscale (about 3 Iron Ingot), Cinderforge (about 4 Iron Ingot), Stillbarrow (about 3 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Old Guildhouse
areas.text: The adventurers' guildhouse, half fallen in, its counters and notice boards still standing and its records still in the cellar.

areas.name: Old Shrine
areas.text: A small shrine to a human god nobody here remembers, where monsters come to sit quietly and own up to what they've done.

areas.name: Perch Tower
areas.text: The old bell tower, its roof torn off and its beams turned into perches for anything with wings.

areas.name: Stela's Emporium
areas.text: A narrow bookshop off the main street crammed floor to ceiling with the books the humans left behind, stacks on every step, a brass till on the counter and laughing coming from somewhere behind the shelves.

areas.name: Swap Ground
areas.text: The market: an old square of cracked flagstones where everything is traded for something else, and an ingot settles the rest.

areas.name: The Gangways
areas.text: Rope bridges and plank walks strung between the rooftops, for anything quick and light enough to use them.

areas.name: The Mouth
areas.text: The dungeon's entrance in the middle of town: a ring of worn stone steps going down into a hole wide enough for an ogre, warm air coming up out of it.

areas.name: The Strongroom
areas.text: The old human bank on the main street, iron doors and a vault still standing, where a kobold with a ring of keys keeps whatever monsters leave with her and counts every last nail of it.

areas.name: The Watering Hole
areas.text: A long low drinking hall of sun-bleached boards off the main street, with a hitching rail out front for riding beasts and swinging doors wide enough for an ogre, where everyone who came up out of the dungeon alive drinks to it and settles their arguments outside.

areas.name: The Writing Den
areas.text: A low room under the eaves above the bookshop, crammed with books, candles and ink pots, loose pages stuck to every wall and the ceiling beams scuffed where somebody hangs from them.

locations.name: Drowned Caves
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

Sea caves under the cliffs that flood at high tide and go back further than any tide reaches.

areas.name: Tide Cave
areas.text: A cave half full of sea water, the walls slick, the water running inward instead of out.

locations.name: Dry Wash Spring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-34 · Danger: Severe]

A dry riverbed cutting through the red waste with a spring at the bottom that runs a trickle at night and nothing by day.

areas.name: Wash Bottom
areas.text: The bottom of the dry riverbed, smooth stones, and a damp patch where the spring seeps up after dark.

locations.name: Dry Well Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-8 · Danger: Low]

An empty human farmhouse out in the Basin scrub with its roof still on and a dry well in the yard, the kind of place anything passing through sleeps a night and moves on.

areas.name: Farmyard
areas.text: A weedy yard between the farmhouse and a fallen barn, the round stone well in the middle with a cart wheel jammed in its mouth.

locations.name: Egg Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A bare island covered from shore to shore in seabird nests, the birds screaming and diving at anything that lands, and the egg hunters come out in spring with baskets on their heads.

areas.name: Nesting Ground
areas.text: A rocky island covered in white seabirds and their nests, eggs in every hollow, sea all round.

locations.name: Elder Dragon Roosts
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Huge curved ribs of rock over the hills where the oldest drakes in the world sleep, drakes so old and big the ghouls call them dragons, and nothing wants to argue the name. They came down after the humans left and took the high ground, and when one wakes and flies the whole kingdom goes quiet.

areas.name: Rib Ledges
areas.text: Ledges under the curved rock ribs, scorched and scattered with huge bones.

locations.name: Falls Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A stone bridge across the top of the falls with the water going under it and straight off the edge. Everything crossing the south of the human land comes over it, and the lizardfolk fish from the rail.

areas.name: Fishing Rail
areas.text: The bridge rail worn smooth where the lizardfolk lean to fish.

locations.name: Falls Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A camp of red tents at the bottom of the keep's road where travellers wait to be let up to the keep or across to the waterhold, and get robbed while they wait.

areas.name: Waiting Tents
areas.text: Red tents at the foot of the keep road, packs piled outside.

locations.name: Falls Ledge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A wide rock shelf halfway down a run of waterfalls where the Lost Human Kingdom's river drops into the jungle, dry, flat and easy to hold, and loud enough that you have to shout to be heard over the water.

areas.name: Dry Cave
areas.text: A cave behind the falls, dry inside, the water a white curtain over the mouth.

areas.name: Falls Stair
areas.text: A path of wet rock steps going down beside the falls from one pool to the next.

areas.name: Spray Shelf
areas.text: A broad flat rock shelf beside a tall waterfall, spray hanging over it and jungle all round.

locations.name: Fen Ruin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High]

A drowned stone hut on a peat bank, the roof gone and the walls full of slime. Something lives in the bottom of it and the fen folk throw scraps in to keep it there.

areas.name: Slime Pit
areas.text: The flooded floor of the hut, thick with slime.

locations.name: First Hall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-2 · Danger: Low]

The first floor under the Mouth: wide stone halls lit by glowing moss, slime pits, goblin squatters and mimics that look like everything. The stone is warm and grows back where it's cut, and every fresh spawn in the Basin has stood on the Entry Stair wondering if it's tough enough to keep going.

areas.name: Entry Stair
areas.text: The worn stair down from the Mouth into the first hall, moss glowing on the walls.

areas.name: Goblin Squat
areas.text: A side hall the goblins have walled off with junk and call theirs, a cookfire going and a toll for passing.

areas.name: Lost Pack Pile
areas.text: A side room heaped with packs, boots and gear the adventurers dropped running out, and half the pile is mimics that look like it.

areas.name: Mimic Gallery
areas.text: A long gallery of chests, doors and statues; some of them are real.

areas.name: Slime Pits
areas.text: A hall of round pits full of slime, bubbling, things half dissolved inside.

locations.name: Floe Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A dark sea full of drifting ice floes off the foot of the glacier, and the only way across is jumping from one to the next, if you're fast, lucky and nothing comes up from under to see what's making the noise.

areas.name: Floe Jump
areas.text: Flat white ice floes floating on a dark blue sea, gaps of black water between them.

locations.name: Floe Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A shelf of rock at the foot of the cliffs where boats and merfolk come in out of the swell, with a wooden pier frozen solid into it. It's the only safe place to land on the whole coast.

areas.name: Frozen Pier
areas.text: A wooden pier frozen solid into the rock shelf.

locations.name: Flooded Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 26-28 · Danger: High]

The first floor of the water road: deep halls drowned in black water, halls you have to swim through, things moving under you in the dark.

areas.name: Air Pocket
areas.text: A dome of trapped air above the water, just big enough to breathe and wait.

areas.name: Black Water
areas.text: A hall flooded to the ceiling but for a gap of air, the water still and black and cold.

areas.name: Drowned Stair
areas.text: A stair going down into black water, and on a still day you can see it keeps going a long way under.

areas.name: Sunk Pillars
areas.text: A drowned hall of pillars, their tops just breaking the surface, slick with weed.

locations.name: Fresh Spring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

A spring of fresh water bubbling up out of a cave on a bare island, the only fresh water in the south of the isles. Whoever holds the island holds the isles, and it changes hands most summers.

areas.name: Spring Cave
areas.text: A small cave where fresh water bubbles up through the sand.

locations.name: Frog Pools
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

Warm green pools in the jungle full of frogs as big as cows, croaking so loud you can't hear yourself, and the snakes that eat them lying along every branch over the water.

areas.name: Lily Water
areas.text: Warm green pools covered in giant lily pads under the jungle trees, huge frogs sitting on the pads.

locations.name: Frost Giant Shorehold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

The frost ogres' second hold, a fortress of blue ice on the cliffs over the sea with a stair cut down to the shore, built to watch the water. The ogres up here fish through the ice with spears longer than a boat, and they don't like strangers on their stair.

areas.name: Shore Stair
areas.text: A stair cut down the ice cliff to the shore, wide enough for ogres.

locations.name: Frost Giant Siegehold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A fortress of black ice blocks the frost ogres built at the top of the hills when they came down off the Rimelands to take the orchard, and never finished taking it. They call themselves giants and they built it giant-sized, doors you could drive a beetle caravan through and steps a bearkin has to climb with both hands. The ogres sit up here watching the white trees through the winter and come down when the blossom comes out.

areas.name: Siege Steps
areas.text: Huge black ice steps up to a door big enough to drive a caravan through.

locations.name: Frost Pool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A ring of ice blocks round a pool that never freezes, the water black and still and warm enough to steam. Drink it and you're warm for a day. Fall in and you don't come up.

areas.name: Steaming Pool
areas.text: A ring of ice blocks round still black water that steams in the cold.

locations.name: Frozen Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

An ogre hunting camp left in a hurry, hide tents still up, spears still in the rack, a pot frozen solid over a fire that went out a long time ago, and nobody came back for any of it.

areas.name: Tent Ring
areas.text: A ring of snow-crusted hide tents round a dead fire pit, a pot frozen on its tripod, spears in a rack.

locations.name: Frozen Falls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-26 · Danger: High]

A waterfall frozen solid down a cliff on the cold side of the Spine, a wall of blue ice taller than Hivehold's gates, and there's a cave behind it you can only get to by climbing the ice.

areas.name: Ice Wall
areas.text: A frozen waterfall hanging down a grey cliff in a wall of blue ice, a dark cave mouth behind it.

locations.name: Gallows Oak
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

A dead oak on a rise in the Basin with old human rope still hanging off its branches, and every monster that passes ties something on for luck, a feather, a tooth, a bit of rag, so the whole tree rattles when the wind comes through.

areas.name: Under the Oak
areas.text: Bare trampled ground round the dead oak's roots, the branches overhead hung with rope ends, bones and rags.

locations.name: Gargoyle Chapel
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A ruined human chapel on a hill with its roof gone and gargoyles still sitting on its walls. Stone walls, a well and a crypt underneath: good bones for a holding.

areas.name: Chapel Nave
areas.text: A roofless nave, pews rotted to nothing, gargoyles watching from the walls.

locations.name: Ghoul Pantry
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-10 · Danger: Low]

The ghouls of the Upper Halls bring their meat here to hang until it's soft enough for them, and you smell this floor two halls before you reach it. They're polite about it. They'll still put you on a hook if you're lying down.

areas.name: Bone Midden
areas.text: Where the ghouls throw what they can't eat, a heap of cracked bones taller than a troll with the rats working it.

areas.name: Cold Larder
areas.text: A cave kept cold by a draft from below, salted things stacked to the roof.

areas.name: Ghoul Kitchen
areas.text: A low room with a long stone table, knives laid out neat, and a pot that never goes off the boil.

areas.name: Meat Hooks
areas.text: Rows of iron hooks from the ceiling, most of them full.

locations.name: Ghoul Warrens
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-32 · Danger: High]

Tunnels dug between the barrows where the wild ghouls live, the ones Stillbarrow won't let through its gates, and they come out at night to dig at the old graves and fight each other over what they find.

areas.name: Warren Mouth
areas.text: A dark hole dug into the side of a grassy barrow, bones scattered round it and claw marks in the earth.

locations.name: Giant's Stair
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A stair of cut ice blocks as tall as a troll each, climbing out of the Spine's north side into the white, built by the frost ogres up here, who call themselves giants and wanted to come south and never did. Their camp still burns at the top, and they don't mind company if it brings meat.

areas.name: Giants' Fire
areas.text: A fire the size of a house in a ring of stone seats, the frost ogres sitting round it roasting whole beasts.

areas.name: Ice Gate
areas.text: Two pillars of blue ice at the top of the stair, carved with huge ogre faces that watch the south.

areas.name: Stair Foot
areas.text: The bottom of the ice stair on the north face of the Spine, where everything that crosses stops to breathe.

locations.name: Glacier Face
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A wall of blue ice where the Rimelands' glaciers run into the sea, taller than Hivehold, with a ledge along the top wide enough to camp on if you don't mind the whole thing creaking under you all night.

areas.name: Crack Line
areas.text: A long deep crack in the ice back from the edge, blue all the way down, wind moaning through it.

areas.name: Ice Steps
areas.text: Steps cut into the ice cliff going down to the water, old and worn, by something with very big feet.

areas.name: Top Ledge
areas.text: A flat ledge of packed snow along the top of a towering blue ice cliff, the sea far below.

locations.name: Glass Flats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A stretch of desert where the sand has melted into sheets of green glass, good glass for anyone who can cut it and carry it.

areas.name: Glass Sheet
areas.text: Green glass running flat to the horizon, cracked in plates, sand blowing over it.

locations.name: Glowcap Dell
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A hollow in the Deep Wood carpeted with glowing mushrooms, bright enough at night to see your own hands by, where travellers camp because the things that hunt in the dark don't like the light.

areas.name: Glow Floor
areas.text: The floor of the dell, soft with glowing caps, old fire scars where travellers have camped in the middle.

locations.name: Golem Graveyard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 19-21 · Danger: Moderate]

The dungeon makes golems on this floor out of whatever it has lying round, stone and bone and old human iron, and most of them come out wrong. The broken ones pile up in heaps that still twitch.

areas.name: Core Forge
areas.text: A pit of glowing stone where new golem cores are cooked in the dungeon's heat.

areas.name: Scrap Heaps
areas.text: Mountains of broken golem limbs, some of them still trying to crawl.

areas.name: Spare Parts
areas.text: A heap of arms, heads and legs from broken golems, stone and iron and bone, and some of the hands still clench.

areas.name: Walking Wall
areas.text: A wall that's really a golem lying down, its face half sunk in the floor.

locations.name: Grave Road Shrine
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-28 · Danger: High]

A small stone shrine on the road into the Barrow Hills where the living leave something for the dead, and the dead leave them alone for it.

areas.name: Offering Step
areas.text: The stone step in front of the shrine, covered in small offerings: bone charms, dried flowers, a few ingot scraps.

locations.name: Grey Cave
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A cave in a grey rock outcrop at the jungle's edge, the only grey rock for miles. The arachne think it's theirs and so does everything that's ever tried to sleep there.

areas.name: Silk Floor
areas.text: The cave floor thick with old silk and husks.

locations.name: Groaning Crags
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

Crags of ice and black rock that groan when the tide moves the floes against them. Drakes sleep in the hollows and hate being woken.

areas.name: Sleeping Hollows
areas.text: Hollows in the crags where the ice has worn the rock smooth.

locations.name: Gull Crags
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

Black crags in a ring of little islands, white with bird mess and loud with them. Harpies come here to eat and the crags are covered in what they don't.

areas.name: Feeding Rocks
areas.text: Flat rocks white with mess and scattered with picked bones.

locations.name: Gull Rock
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A sea stack off the cliffs, white with gull muck and so loud with birds you can't hear yourself, where the crabfolk climb out at low tide for eggs.

areas.name: Egg Ledges
areas.text: The ledges up the side of the stack, slick with muck and packed with nests, the sea crashing below.

locations.name: Hanging Stones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A ring of tall standing stones on a grey hilltop with old iron chains hanging off every one, the ends broken, and nobody in the hills knows what was chained there or where it went.

areas.name: Chain Ring
areas.text: A ring of grey standing stones on a bare hill, rusted chains hanging from each with their ends torn open.

locations.name: Harpy Crags
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-28 · Danger: High]

Broken peaks on the Spine crusted white with harpy nests, the screaming going all day, and anything that climbs past them gets dive-bombed, robbed and laughed at all the way back down.

areas.name: Harpy Ledges
areas.text: Narrow ledges on a jagged peak covered in big messy nests of sticks and bones, feathers caught on every rock.

locations.name: High Spring
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A spring coming out of a ring of carved stone up on the high ground, falling down to the river in a waterfall. The water's clean and cold, and there's always a hydra close enough to hear you drink.

areas.name: Carved Ring
areas.text: A ring of carved stone round the spring's mouth.

locations.name: Hill Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A carved marker stone at the edge of the pines, the kind the humans put up at the edge of their land, worn smooth on the side the wind hits. Bearkin rub their backs on it and fox spirits leave little stacks of pebbles on top, and nobody knows why they both do it.

areas.name: Pebble Stacks
areas.text: Little stacks of pebbles on top of a worn standing stone.

locations.name: Hivehold
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 15-30 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

An antfolk city carved into a whole mountain: galleries, roads and halls running up inside the peak, millions of feet on the move. Outsiders are allowed in the guest ledge and the ore galleries and nowhere else.

areas.name: Aphid Pastures
areas.text: A warm gallery lit by glowing fungus where the antfolk keep herds of fat green aphids and milk them for honeydew.

areas.name: Dead Chamber
areas.text: A deep chamber where the hive carries its dead, stacked neat and dry, and the workers come back for them when the hive is hungry.

areas.name: Fungus Farms
areas.text: Long warm galleries where the hive grows its food on beds of chewed leaves.

areas.name: Guest Ledge
areas.text:
A wide ledge cut into the mountainside where outsiders are met, traded with and watched.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Rattle Warren (about 4 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Hatch Tunnels
areas.text: Warm tunnels deep in the hive where the young are raised; closed to outsiders.

areas.name: Ore Galleries
areas.text: Long galleries where antfolk workers haul ore out of the mountain in endless lines.

areas.name: Queen's Gallery
areas.text: The great hall at the heart of the mountain where the queen lies; nobody from outside has seen it.

areas.name: Soldier Galleries
areas.text: Galleries where the soldiers drill in silence and every outsider is watched.

areas.name: Trade Chamber
areas.text: A round chamber off the guest ledge where the hive's traders bargain with outsiders through a grille.

areas.name: Upper Vents
areas.text: Vents near the peak where hot air from the hive pours out into the cold.

areas.name: Waste Shafts
areas.text: Deep shafts where the hive drops everything it can't use, and things live at the bottom.

areas.name: Worker Roads
areas.text: Wide roads inside the mountain packed with antfolk workers moving in lines that never break.

locations.name: Hornmoot
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 5-16 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A trading camp in the long grass round a standing stone with horns carved in it, where the herds meet. Centaurs, minotaurs and boarfolk come in to trade hides, meat and stock, and the gnolls come in pretending they aren't there to steal.

areas.name: Bone Carvers
areas.text: A row of awnings where horn and bone are carved into tools, charms and trade tokens.

areas.name: Calving Ground
areas.text: A fenced field on the camp's edge where the herds bring their young, guarded day and night by the biggest minotaurs.

areas.name: Elders' Fire
areas.text: A fire that never goes out at the camp's heart, where each herd's eldest sits and nobody else does.

areas.name: Herd Pens
areas.text:
Fenced pens of stock on the camp's edge where the caravans load and the beetles graze.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Delvers' Rest (about 3 Iron Ingot), Saltreef (about 3 Iron Ingot), Ringgrove (about 2 Iron Ingot), Cinderforge (about 3 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Hide Market
areas.text: Racks of stretched hides and piles of furs, horn and hoof, the herds' trade laid out on the grass.

areas.name: Hoof Smithy
areas.text: A big open tent with an anvil and a fire where the farrier shoes centaurs and minotaurs, both holding very still and both hating it.

areas.name: Horn Stone
areas.text: The great standing stone in the middle, horns carved deep into it, polished by every hand that has sworn on it.

areas.name: Moot Ring
areas.text: A wide ring of standing stones round the horn stone, where disputes are shouted out and settled.

areas.name: Racing Ground
areas.text: A long strip of trampled grass where the centaurs race and the whole camp bets on it.

areas.name: Smoke Tents
areas.text: Low tents full of smoke where meat is cured and the old ones sit telling the same stories.

areas.name: Tent Rows
areas.text: Rows of hide tents, every herd with its own colours on the poles.

areas.name: Trough Line
areas.text: A long line of water troughs dug into the grass, every herd taking its turn and arguing about it.

locations.name: Hot Spring Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A valley in the white where hot springs keep the ground green and the snow off, the only warm ground for days in any direction. Whoever holds it can winter through anything.

areas.name: Steam Pools
areas.text: Steaming pools in a green hollow, snow piled high on every ridge round it.

locations.name: Hunter's Hang
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A lone dead tree in the grass with meat hung high in its branches on hide ropes, where the centaur hunters keep their kills out of reach of the gnolls until the carts come.

areas.name: Hang Tree
areas.text: The foot of the dead tree, hide ropes running up to the meat, the grass round it trampled and dark with old blood.

locations.name: Hydra Pools
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-24 · Danger: High]

Deep black pools in the middle of the fen, where the hydras live. The water steams and nothing grows on the banks.

areas.name: Steaming Bank
areas.text: A bare mud bank over black water that steams, bones half sunk in the mud.

locations.name: Ice Arch
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 38-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A cave right through the glacier where the sea comes in underneath it, the light coming through the ice blue as a gem, and something big lives in the back of it and drags its kills in on the tide.

areas.name: Sea Cave
areas.text: A blue ice cave with seawater running into it, light shining through the ice walls, bones on a ledge.

locations.name: Ice Ruin
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

The half-buried top of an ice fortress older than the stair, most of it still under the snow, the door at the top just big enough to crawl through. Something keeps the snow cleared off the door.

areas.name: Crawl Door
areas.text: A small door at the top of a buried wall, the snow round it swept clear.

locations.name: Ice Wreck
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A ship frozen into the floe, mast snapped, its ribs sticking up out of the ice like a carcass. Merfolk swim in under it to get at the hold, and the hold still has something in it worth the cold.

areas.name: Frozen Hold
areas.text: The ship's hold under the ice, reached from below by swimming.

locations.name: Imp Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 21-23 · Danger: High]

Imps come up from the Lower Depths to trade on this floor, and everything they sell is either stolen, cursed or a lie. It's also the only place in the dungeon you can buy a map that's true this week.

areas.name: Back Room
areas.text: The room behind the stalls where the real goods are kept, the stolen things that would get an imp killed if anyone saw them out front.

areas.name: Brass Cage
areas.text: A big brass cage in the middle of the market where the imps keep whatever they caught this week.

areas.name: Lie Stalls
areas.text: Rickety stalls of smoking trinkets, every imp swearing on its mother that it's genuine.

areas.name: Smoke Ring
areas.text: A ring of braziers where deals are sealed in smoke that smells like burnt hair.

locations.name: Iron Seam
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-28 · Danger: High]

A thick seam of iron ore showing in a cliff face high in the Spine, easy to dig and close enough to a pass to haul out.

areas.name: Seam Face
areas.text: A cliff face streaked red-black with ore, a ledge under it wide enough to work.

locations.name: Iron Stakes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A line of iron stakes driven into the ground right across the Iron March, new iron, not rusted, and nobody saw who put them there or heard the hammering.

areas.name: Stake Line
areas.text: A straight line of shiny iron stakes running away across the grass to the horizon, a few with rags tied on.

locations.name: Islet Maze
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

Hundreds of little green islets with water running between them every way at once, each one looking just like the last, and boats go in and come out a day later wondering where the day went.

areas.name: Green Islets
areas.text: Little green islets of mangrove and sand with bright blue channels winding between them.

locations.name: Jade Dig
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A stepped pyramid of green stone cut open on one side where mantids and lizardfolk dig out green stone to carve. They're digging it out of the pyramid itself, and every layer they cut deeper the carvings get older.

areas.name: Cut Face
areas.text: The pyramid's cut-open side, carvings in every layer.

locations.name: Keep Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A ring of standing stones under the keep's walls where the lizardfolk leave offerings so the dead stay up there. The offerings are gone by morning.

areas.name: Offering Ring
areas.text: Offerings laid inside a ring of standing stones under the keep wall.

locations.name: Kennels of Ash
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 27-29 · Danger: High]

Where the hellhounds sleep and breed, ash knee-deep and warm, bones gnawed white in every corner. A pack can smell a soul from the other end of the floor, and an Aberrant smells like a feast.

areas.name: Ash Kennels
areas.text: Hollows scooped in deep warm ash, each one a pack's bed, ringed with bones.

areas.name: Gnaw Yard
areas.text: A yard of bones gnawed to points, where the pups fight and learn.

areas.name: Howling Shaft
areas.text: A shaft going straight down where the howls of the lower packs come up.

areas.name: Whelping Den
areas.text: A deep warm den in the ash where the hellhound mothers keep their litters, and they don't let anything near.

locations.name: Kobold Kilns
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-12 · Danger: Low]

A row of brick kilns dug into a Greenhill hillside, where the kobolds fire pots, bricks and the clay parts of their traps, smoke going up all day and the kobolds yelling at anything that walks too close to a firing.

areas.name: Kiln Row
areas.text: Round brick kilns set into the hill in a line, smoke coming out the tops, stacks of fired pots drying in the sun.

locations.name: Kraken Deep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A black reef over water so deep it goes dark a few feet down, where the boats go round the long way, and the ones that don't come back as wreckage.

areas.name: Black Reef
areas.text: A black reef breaking the surface over water that goes dark straight down, wreckage caught on the rocks.

locations.name: Landing Reeds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High]

Reeds round a wooden landing on stilts where the boats from Stiltscale tie up, the reeds cut back so nothing can come up close without being seen.

areas.name: Stilt Landing
areas.text: A wooden landing on stilts with boats tied up.

locations.name: Last Fort
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The biggest of the empty human forts on the ridge at the west edge of the Wildreach: walls still standing, gates hanging open, barracks full of rusted kit. Monsters avoid it out of habit. Some of them have started avoiding it for new reasons.

areas.name: Armoury
areas.text: The fort's armoury, racks of human spears and shields still standing in rows, most of the good stuff long since carried off.

areas.name: Barracks
areas.text: Long rooms of rotted bunks and rusted gear, and one corner swept clean.

areas.name: Fort Chapel
areas.text: A small chapel with a human god's sign over the altar and fresh wax on the candles.

areas.name: Gatehouse
areas.text: The fort's gatehouse, the portcullis rusted half up, arrow slits looking west.

areas.name: Mess Hall
areas.text: A long hall of tables and benches with the bowls still laid out, dust thick on everything, set for a meal nobody came to.

areas.name: Wall Walk
areas.text: The top of the wall, looking west over the old roads into the human lands.

areas.name: Well Yard
areas.text: A yard in the middle of the fort with a deep stone well, the bucket still on its rope and the water still sweet.

locations.name: Leaning Post
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

An old human signpost at the crossroads in the middle of the Basin, leaning so far over it points at the dirt, every board scratched over with monster marks saying which road goes where and what's waiting down it.

areas.name: The Crossroads
areas.text: Four dirt roads meeting at the leaning signpost, rutted by beetle carts, a flat stone beside it worn smooth by everything that's sat there.

locations.name: Ledge Shelter
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: High]

A shelter cut under an overhang on a high ledge of the Spine, a firepit and a stack of dry wood kept by whoever used it last for whoever comes next.

areas.name: Under the Overhang
areas.text: The dry space under the rock, a firepit, the woodpile against the back wall and fresh claw marks above it.

locations.name: Leech Ditch
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A long drowned ditch across the fen that's the only way through for a mile either side, chest-deep for an orc and over the head of a goblin, and everything that wades it comes out lighter than it went in.

areas.name: The Wade
areas.text: A long straight channel of black water between reed banks, ripples moving under the surface.

locations.name: Lich Terrace Keep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A white keep of terraces and towers at the top of the falls where the human dead of the south went to be buried, and stayed up. The skeletons there serve a dead lord the lizardfolk call the Lich, a skeleton in a crown, and the keep's gates open for anyone who comes to it carrying a body.

areas.name: Body Gate
areas.text: The keep's main gate, which opens only for someone carrying a body.

locations.name: Lich War Chapel
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A grey stone chapel the humans built for their war dead, with black spires and the old army's names cut into the walls. The skeletons that walk out of its crypt answer to one of their own the hill folk call the Lich, a soldier's skeleton older than the rest that still gives orders in a language nobody living speaks. The fox spirits won't go near it after dark.

areas.name: Crypt Stair
areas.text: A stone stair going down under the chapel floor into the crypt, cold air coming up it.

locations.name: Light Wreck
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

A ship broken on the rocks under Wreckers' Light, one of the ones the light brought in. The wreckers stripped it, and they keep it there on purpose to show the next ship where not to go, which is exactly where they want them.

areas.name: Picked Ribs
areas.text: The wreck's ribs stripped bare on the rocks.

locations.name: Lighthouse Stump
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A broken human lighthouse on the rocks, the top half gone into the sea and the stair inside still climbing round and round to nothing, and the gulls own everything above the tenth step.

areas.name: Broken Stair
areas.text: A spiral stone stair inside a roofless lighthouse tower, open to the sky, the sea crashing on rocks below.

locations.name: Long Sandbar
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A long white sandbar out among the isles that only shows at low tide, covered in shells as big as carts.

areas.name: Shell Rows
areas.text: The middle of the sandbar, the huge empty shells lying in neat rows like something laid them out.

locations.name: Low Tide Cave
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

A sea cave in a green island where the tide runs in and out, dry for an hour at low water. The sharkfolk keep things in it they don't want found, and they come back for them at the next low tide.

areas.name: Dry Hour
areas.text: The back of the cave, dry for an hour at low water, crates wedged in the rock.

locations.name: Mammoth Trail
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A frozen valley the mammoth herds walk every year, the snow beaten down into a road a hundred feet wide, and the frost ogres wait at the narrow end with spears for the slow ones.

areas.name: Beaten Snow
areas.text: A wide road of trampled snow down a white valley between icy hills, huge round footprints in it.

locations.name: Mangrove Reeds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A bed of reeds at the edge of the mangroves where the delta's crabfolk lay their eggs. They don't leave them alone, and they don't leave visitors alone either.

areas.name: Egg Beds
areas.text: Clutches of crab eggs tucked in the reed roots.

locations.name: Merfolk Tidehold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A hall of white curved arches the merfolk grew up out of the sea ice, half in the water, where they come up to trade fish and old human things off the sea floor for metal. The hall melts a little more every year and they keep growing it back.

areas.name: Trading Pool
areas.text: A pool inside the white arches where the merfolk surface to trade.

locations.name: Mill Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A stone bridge over the mill stream on the main road south, with a toll house on one end nobody's sat in for a generation. Golems still stand at the toll house, waiting for the coin.

areas.name: Toll House
areas.text: A small stone toll house at the bridge end, golems stood by its door.

locations.name: Moss Circle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

A ring of old stones gone green under the moss in a quiet part of the wood, where the treants come and stand still for days at a time, and if you stand still long enough with them they start to talk.

areas.name: Stone Ring
areas.text: A circle of mossy standing stones in a clearing, ferns round them and old trees leaning in.

locations.name: North Cliffs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

Sea cliffs on the egg island's south side where the crabfolk climb up out of the water to get at the eggs, and the harpies drop rocks on them for it. It's been going on longer than anyone can remember.

areas.name: Egg Climb
areas.text: The cliff face scored by crab claws, eggs in the ledges above.

locations.name: North Gate Ruin
locations.info:
