[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A ruined gatehouse at the north end of the kingdom's road, the gates fallen in and grown over. Wraiths stand guard in it for a king who isn't coming back.

areas.name: Fallen Gates
areas.text: The gates fallen in under the arch and grown over with ivy.

locations.name: Obelisk Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The bottom of the road, a wide stone stair coming up out of the Rimelands snow to a landing between two white obelisks with a gold sun on each, and nobody living remembers who set them there, only that the snow never settles on the steps. Frost ogres come this far to leave meat on the bottom step and go no further, because the ones that did go further came back down without their names, and the drakes that fly over the Rimelands turn wide around it. The sylphs come down to the landing at dusk to look at whoever is waiting, and whoever is waiting has usually been waiting a while.

areas.name: The Arch Seats
areas.text: Stone arches built into the obelisk bases, out of the wind, where travellers sit and wait for the road to let them on.

areas.name: The Bottom Step
areas.text: The first step out of the snow, worn smooth, a heap of frozen meat and old bones on it that the ogres keep topping up.

areas.name: The Two Obelisks
areas.text: The white stones either side of the landing, a gold sun cut into each, warm to touch in the cold.

locations.name: Ogre Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A stone bridge over a frozen gully, wide and low and built by ogres, with a toll in frozen meat. Pay it or go round, and round is two days.

areas.name: Meat Toll
areas.text: Frozen meat hung on hooks at the bridge end, the toll for crossing.

locations.name: Ogre Ford
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A shallow crossing on the river through Greenhill with a big flat rock beside it, where an ogre sits and charges everybody to cross. Whoever holds the rock holds the road.

areas.name: Toll Rock
areas.text: A flat boulder over the ford with a seat worn into it and a stack of skulls beside it for decoration.

locations.name: Old Oak
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A single oak so wide a house could stand inside its trunk, alone in a clearing, with good dry hollows in it and acorns the size of fists.

areas.name: Oak Hollow
areas.text: A dry room inside the oak's trunk, smelling of wood and rain, with a knot-hole for a window.

locations.name: Old Road Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A camp beside the old west road where somebody has been sleeping lately: a cold fire ring, a lean-to of timber pulled off the forts and prints in the ash.

areas.name: Fire Ring
areas.text: The cold fire ring and the lean-to beside it, the ash trodden with boot prints, all of them going west.

locations.name: Old Watch
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A watch house of ice blocks on the road out to the springs, roof gone, the fire pit still black. Travellers shelter here, and leave the frozen dead where they find them because nobody can dig a grave up here.

areas.name: Fire Pit
areas.text: A black fire pit inside roofless ice walls, frozen dead sat round it.

locations.name: Open Barrow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

A grave mound broken open from the inside, its stone door pushed out flat and the earth round it scored with claw marks.

areas.name: Broken Mouth
areas.text: The broken front of the mound, the stone slab lying flat, the passage inside going down into the dark.

locations.name: Orchard Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human farm up in the foothills under the snow, the field still ploughed in rows and the gate still shut, and nobody left to work it, the first flat ground for days where a band could dig in and hold.

areas.name: Farm Gate
areas.text: A wooden farm gate on the hill road, a ploughed field behind it in neat brown rows and pines all round.

areas.name: Farmhouse
areas.text: A low stone farmhouse at the top of the field with its shutters closed and a cold hearth inside.

areas.name: Ploughed Rows
areas.text: The farm's one big field, ploughed in straight rows and planted with something that hasn't come up yet.

locations.name: Peat Island
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A dry island of peat in the fen with a ruined stone hut on it, good ground to cut fuel and hold.

areas.name: Ruined Hut
areas.text: A stone hut with half a roof on a hump of peat, reeds all round it.

locations.name: Peat Reeds
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High]

A bed of reeds round Peat Island where the lizardfolk cut peat to burn, and where the trolls come up out of the water to watch them do it.

areas.name: Peat Cuts
areas.text: Square cuts in the peat bank, stacks of drying peat beside them.

locations.name: Plague Pits
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Long filled-in trenches in the fields outside an empty village, the ground sunk in long lines where the humans buried their dead in the plague, and nothing grows on them, not even weeds.

areas.name: Sunk Lines
areas.text: Long sunken lines of bare grey earth in a weedy field, an empty stone village behind them.

locations.name: Plunge Pools
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-40 · Danger: Severe]

Deep green pools at the bottom of the falls where the river goes into the Deepgreen, so deep nobody has touched the bottom, and the jungle crowding right down to the water.

areas.name: Bottom Pools
areas.text: Deep green pools under the last waterfall, jungle crowding the rocks round them, mist over the water.

locations.name: Ratrun
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-4 · Danger: Low]

A floor gone to the ratfolk: the halls are too big for them so they've dug their own little tunnels through the walls, and you hear them all round you the whole time, scratching and squeaking and laughing at something you can't see.

areas.name: Nest Burrows
areas.text: A warren of shredded cloth and paper in a collapsed hall, warm and stinking, full of young.

areas.name: Rat Holes
areas.text: A wall riddled with round holes at ankle height, eyes in half of them.

areas.name: Rat King's Nest
areas.text: A nest of straw and stolen cloth behind the walls where the ratfolk's oldest sits on a pile of everything the others brought him.

areas.name: Squeak Market
areas.text: A low hall where the ratfolk swap stolen things on blankets and scatter at any loud noise.

locations.name: Rattle Warren
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 1-12 · Danger: Low · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A goblin and kobold town dug into three hills, so loud you hear it a mile off: tin bells on every tunnel, kids screaming, hammers going and somebody always arguing over a price. It's dirty, crowded and the cheapest place in the Wildreach to buy junk that almost works.

areas.name: Bell Tunnels
areas.text: The main tunnels between the hills, tin bells strung on every beam so the whole warren hears who's coming.

areas.name: Brat Pits
areas.text: Muddy pits where the goblin young fight each other over scraps while the adults bet on who comes out.

areas.name: Chief's Mound
areas.text: The top of the biggest hill, where the chief sits on a pile of loot and anyone can fight for the seat.

areas.name: Gob Kitchen
areas.text: A low smoky cave full of cook pots on fires, goblins shouting over every one of them, the stew made of whatever came in that day.

areas.name: Junk Market
areas.text:
A long trench market under hide awnings, piled with scrap, traps, half-made tools and things nobody can name.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Delvers' Rest (about 2 Iron Ingot), Hivehold (about 4 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Kobold Dig
areas.text: The kobold side of the warren: neat tunnels, gem lamps and a shrine to a drake carved in the wall.

areas.name: Lookout Chimney
areas.text: A narrow shaft cut up through the hill to a hole in the top, a goblin up there all day with a bell, watching the roads.

areas.name: Scrap Forge
areas.text: A smoky hole where goblins hammer junk into weapons that work about half the time.

areas.name: Stink Pond
areas.text: A green pond at the bottom of the hills where the warren throws everything it doesn't want, and some things it does.

areas.name: The Third Hill
areas.text: The hill the kobolds dug into and won't talk about, its tunnel mouths bricked shut and a kobold sat at each one.

areas.name: Trader's Hole
areas.text: A burrow with a counter cut into the wall, where outsiders can buy without going any deeper into the warren.

areas.name: Trap Run
areas.text: The tunnel into town, lined with traps the locals step round without looking and strangers don't.

locations.name: Red Keep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-34 · Danger: Severe]

A keep of red stone on the highest hill, its windows shuttered, its gate open, and nobody who goes in by night coming out.

areas.name: Keep Hall
areas.text: A long hall lit by red candles, a feast laid out that nobody has eaten, a chair at the end.

locations.name: Red Tent Camp
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A cluster of red tents pitched in the lee of the chapel wall where hunters and scavengers camp before they go up into the hills. The tents are old human army tents, taken off the dead and patched, and nobody who sleeps in them sleeps well.

areas.name: Patched Tents
areas.text: Old red army tents patched with hide, a cold firepit between them.

locations.name: Reed Platform
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A raft of lashed reeds the size of a house tied to a dead tree in a fen channel, where lizardfolk boatmen stop to rest, trade fish and wait out the fog.

areas.name: Reed Deck
areas.text: The top of the reed raft, springy underfoot, a smoke-blackened fire tray in the middle and boats tied all round the edge.

locations.name: Reed Shallows
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Reeds standing in the shallows of the brown river where the hydras come to drink. Mandrakes grow in the mud between them and scream when they're pulled.

areas.name: Mandrake Mud
areas.text: Mud between the reeds where mandrakes grow.

locations.name: Reef Wreck
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

A ship torn open on the reef, its cargo spilled across the rocks and picked clean years ago. Sharkfolk use the hull as a lookout for the next one.

areas.name: Lookout Hull
areas.text: The ship's broken hull on the reef, a lookout perch on the high end.

locations.name: Ringgrove
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 5-20 · Danger: Moderate · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A town grown rather than built: a ring of huge trees with homes in their trunks and branches, bridges of living wood between them, mushroom halls at their roots. Dryads, treants, myconids and fox spirits live here, and none of them like axes.

areas.name: Bark Market
areas.text: Stalls grown into the side of a trunk selling herbs, honey, sap and mushrooms.

areas.name: Branch Bridges
areas.text: Living branches grown into walkways between the great trees, high above the forest floor.

areas.name: Dryad Pools
areas.text: Clear pools between the roots where the dryads bathe and nobody stares if they want to keep their eyes.

areas.name: Fox Shrine
areas.text: A small red shrine in the hollow of a tree, always with something left on it, always taken by morning.

areas.name: Leaf Loft
areas.text: A platform high in the branches roofed with living leaves, where travellers sleep in hammocks and wake up covered in pixies.

areas.name: Pixie Hollow
areas.text: A glowing hollow full of tiny houses in the bark, buzzing and giggling, where nothing you drop stays yours.

areas.name: Root Steps
areas.text:
Steps grown out of the roots down to the forest road, where the caravans tie up.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Delvers' Rest (about 3 Iron Ingot), Hornmoot (about 2 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Sap House
areas.text: A hollow in a great tree where the dryads tap the sap and sell it in cups, sweet and strong enough to knock out an orc.

areas.name: Seed Store
areas.text: A hollow trunk packed with seeds, nuts and roots against the winter, guarded by squirrels that bite.

areas.name: Spore Hall
areas.text: A great mushroom grown into a hall at the roots, lit soft blue, where the myconids share their dreams.

areas.name: The Ring
areas.text: The clearing inside the ring of trees, soft with moss, where the grove holds its gatherings.

areas.name: Treant Circle
areas.text: A ring of old treants standing so still they look like trees, where the grove's oldest law is kept.

locations.name: Riverfork Clearing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A dry clearing where two jungle rivers meet, high enough to stay out of the floods, with timber and fruit all round it. Good ground to build on, if you can keep it.

areas.name: Riverbank
areas.text: A clearing on high ground where two brown rivers meet, jungle walls on every side.

locations.name: Road of Boots
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A wide old road through farmland gone wild, and on it, pressed in the mud, the prints of thousands of boots, all going east.

areas.name: Boot Tracks
areas.text: A muddy road through tall grass, boot prints by the thousand pressed into it, all pointing east.

locations.name: Root Cave
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A cave in the roots of a fallen tree as big as a hill, deep and dark and dry. Arachne spin in the top of it and lizardfolk shelter in the bottom, and they've got a deal nobody else knows the terms of.

areas.name: Hanging Webs
areas.text: The top of the cave hung thick with webs.

locations.name: Root Town
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

An old camp built up in the mangrove roots over the water where the Deepgreen's rivers meet the sea, plank walkways between the trees still holding, and everybody who comes here wonders who built it and where they went.

areas.name: Boat Roots
areas.text: A ring of roots where small boats can tie up, the water deep and calm under the trees.

areas.name: Cook Platform
areas.text: A wide platform of planks in the roots with cold fire pits and pots still hanging over them.

areas.name: Root Walks
areas.text: Plank walkways strung between huge mangrove roots over brown water, huts in the branches.

locations.name: Rope Bridge Gully
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

A deep gully between two Greenhill hills with a goblin rope bridge strung across it, which the goblins cut loose the moment anything big starts over and string back up once it's gone.

areas.name: Bridge Head
areas.text: The near end of the rope bridge, the posts hacked about from every time it's been cut, the gully dropping away under the planks.

locations.name: Rot Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-20 · Danger: Moderate]

A sunken part of the wood where everything is dead and covered in white fungus, and the air is thick with spores.

areas.name: White Floor
areas.text: A floor of white fungus over fallen trees, soft underfoot, spores hanging in the still air.

locations.name: Ruin Terraces
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

Green stone terraces climbing a hill, the ruin of a town older than the humans, overgrown and quiet. The mantids keep it clear of growth and won't say who for.

areas.name: Clear Steps
areas.text: Terrace steps kept clear of every root and vine.

locations.name: Salamander Deeps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 31-33 · Danger: Severe]

Wild salamanders live here, the ones the Cinderforge smiths came from long ago, bathing in pools of molten rock and shedding skins that keep burning for days. They'll trade fire-work for meat and they don't know what a fair price is.

areas.name: Ember Pools
areas.text: Round pools of liquid fire where salamanders lie soaking like it's bathwater.

areas.name: Hot Spring Stair
areas.text: A stair of wet steaming rock where scalding water runs down from somewhere above.

areas.name: Old Forge
areas.text: A forge cut into the rock, long cold, where the first Cinderforge smiths learned the work before they went up.

areas.name: Shed Skins
areas.text: A cave hung with shed salamander skins, still smouldering, lighting the walls red.

locations.name: Salt Lick
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A white salt pan in the grass where every herd comes to lick, and where whoever holds it can cut salt and sell it to everyone.

areas.name: Salt Pan
areas.text: A flat crust of white salt cracked into plates, hoofprints all over it.

locations.name: Saltreef
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A crabfolk and merfolk town on a reef just off the coast, half above the water and half under it. At low tide you can walk out to it; at high tide you swim.

areas.name: Crab Barracks
areas.text: A walled rock pool where the crabfolk guard sharpen their claws and wait for the sharkfolk.

areas.name: Drowned Bell
areas.text: A human ship's bell hung under the reef where it rings with the tide, and the merfolk meet under it to settle deals.

areas.name: Kelp Racks
areas.text: Racks of kelp drying in the sun and wind, the whole reef smelling of it.

areas.name: Lookout Spire
areas.text: A spire of coral at the reef's highest point with a horn to blow when fins are sighted.

areas.name: Molting Pool
areas.text: A sheltered rock pool where the crabfolk go to shed their shells, soft and touchy for days, and nobody else is let in.

areas.name: Pearl Steps
areas.text: Steps cut down into the water where the divers go in after pearls and come out counting.

areas.name: Shell Hall
areas.text: A great hall built inside the shell of something that died long ago, where the reef's council meets.

areas.name: Siren Rocks
areas.text: Black rocks at the end of the reef where the sirens sit and sing, and where nobody sensible goes.

areas.name: The Causeway
areas.text: A path of reef rock out to the town that's dry at low tide and under water at high.

areas.name: Tide Market
areas.text:
A flat shelf of reef where the market is held at low tide and the caravans come down the causeway.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Hornmoot (about 3 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Under Hall
areas.text: The half of the town under the water, a hall of coral where the merfolk meet.

areas.name: Wreck Yard
areas.text: A cove full of broken ships the town strips for timber and iron.

locations.name: Sandworm Field
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

A flat stretch of red sand that moves when nothing's walking on it, slow ripples going across like water, and the caravans go a day out of their way to go round it.

areas.name: Rippling Sand
areas.text: Flat red sand to the horizon with long ripples moving across it, the bleached ribs of a beetle half buried.

locations.name: Scorched Orchard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human orchard burnt black from end to end, rows of dead trees in the ash, except for the far end where a few still fruit, and everything in the March comes to eat the apples.

areas.name: Last Rows
areas.text: The far end of a burnt orchard, a few green trees heavy with red apples among rows of black dead ones.

locations.name: Scorpion Wells
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-34 · Danger: Severe]

Three old wells in a ring of rocks where the scorpids have their nest. The only water for a day in any direction.

areas.name: Well Ring
areas.text: Three stone wells in a ring of red rocks, sand drifted up against them, holes in the sand all round.

locations.name: Scrap Heap Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 2-10 · Danger: Low]

Rattle Warren's tip, a whole hill made of what the warren throws out, broken pots, bent iron, carts, bones and things nobody can name, and every morning the runts are out on it picking over the new stuff before the bigger goblins wake up.

areas.name: The Heap
areas.text: A steep slope of rusted junk, broken wheels and old crates, paths worn across it by small feet.

locations.name: Serpentfolk Root Keep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A round keep of green stone in the mangroves at the top of the delta, built by the lamia when the delta was dry ground, now standing in the tide with the roots growing up its walls. The serpentfolk run the delta from it and every boat that comes down the river pays them.

areas.name: Rooted Walls
areas.text: The keep's walls with mangrove roots grown up through the stones.

locations.name: Serpentfolk Waterhold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A round hold of green stone terraces built round the river below the falls, the lamia's court in the south, the river running through its middle so they can come and go by water. The lamia here call themselves serpentfolk and charge everything on the river for passing them, in goods or in work.

areas.name: Water Gate
areas.text: A gate in the waterhold's wall the river runs through.

locations.name: Shark Run
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-32 · Danger: High]

Long flooded channels where the sharkfolk hunt, fins cutting the black water, the walls scraped by teeth. They come up from the Broken Coast through the Drowned Caves to hunt here, and they don't share.

areas.name: Blood Pool
areas.text: A deep round pool always clouded red, where the hunts end.

areas.name: Fin Channels
areas.text: Long straight channels of black water with ledges along each side.

areas.name: Gut Ledge
areas.text: A ledge above the water where the sharkfolk drag their kills to eat.

areas.name: Tooth Pile
areas.text: A ledge where the sharkfolk spit out their old teeth, a heap of them knee deep and sharp enough to cut boots.

locations.name: Sinkhole Den
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-6 · Danger: Low]

A sinkhole in an old field a short walk from Delvers' Rest, opening into a dry cave big enough for a family of anything. Something always lives in it, and something is always trying to take it.

areas.name: Den Floor
areas.text: The cave floor under the sinkhole, lit by the hole above, dry and soft with old bedding.

locations.name: Smugglers' Atoll
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A ring of reef round a calm lagoon a day's sail east of Saltreef, where every boat that doesn't want to be found ties up. Nobody owns it, everybody uses it, and the only rule is you don't steal from someone tied up next to you.

areas.name: Atoll Dock
areas.text: A long dock of lashed wreck timber in the lagoon, boats of every kind tied up along it.

areas.name: Lagoon Market
areas.text: Stalls on stilts over the shallow lagoon, selling whatever came off whatever ship.

areas.name: Lookout Rock
areas.text: A black rock at the top of the atoll where someone always watches the sea.

locations.name: Snow Bear Den
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A big dry cave under a shelf of red rock where the bearkin sleep out the worst of the snow. Wake one early and the whole den wakes with it.

areas.name: Bear Bedding
areas.text: A dry cave floor heaped with old bedding and bones.

locations.name: Snowline Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 38-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A dirt road winding up through the pines from the farm to where the snow starts, the last bit of the hills before the Rimelands, with old cart ruts frozen into it at the top.

areas.name: Last Bend
areas.text: The top of a winding dirt road where the pines thin out and the snow starts, frozen ruts in the mud.

locations.name: Song Grotto
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 34-36 · Danger: Severe]

Sirens live down here, the deep kind, pale as the dark, singing in a grotto where the water glows faintly blue. The song carries through stone, and monsters walk into the water with smiles on their faces.

areas.name: Deaf Cave
areas.text: A side cave where the siren song can't reach, and the floor is full of everything that ran in to get away from it and never came out.

areas.name: Drowned Bones
areas.text: A pile of bones under the clear water, every skull smiling.

areas.name: Pearl Beds
areas.text: Shallow beds of giant shells, some cracked open on pearls the size of fists.

areas.name: Song Grotto Pool
areas.text: A round grotto of faintly glowing water, rocks round it where the sirens sit.

locations.name: Spider Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 8-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A dip in the Deep Wood roofed over with web so thick it's dark at noon, and whatever walks in feels it before it sees it, the threads going tight and every leg up in the canopy turning to look.

areas.name: Web Roof
areas.text: A shadowed hollow under a ceiling of thick white web strung between the trees, wrapped shapes hanging from it.

locations.name: Split Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A boulder the size of a hall out in the long grass, split clean down the middle, the herds walking single file through the gap like a gate between one grazing and the next.

areas.name: The Gap
areas.text: The narrow way between the two halves of the stone, the grass worn to dirt by hooves, cool shade on both sides.

locations.name: Spray Rock
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-35 · Danger: Severe]

A lump of rock out in the open water that the swell breaks over all day, and a siren sits on it when the tide's right. Ships give it a wide berth now.

areas.name: Singing Ledge
areas.text: A flat ledge on the rock just above the spray where the siren sits.

locations.name: Stair Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A bridge of ice blocks over the melt river below the stair, where everything going between the stair and the hot springs has to cross. The ogres keep a watch on it and the watch is always hungry.

areas.name: Bridge Watch
areas.text: An ice-block watch post at the bridge end with a fire that's never let die.

locations.name: Stampede Scar
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-14 · Danger: Moderate]

A long strip of torn-up ground through the grass where the herds once ran over something all at once, and nothing has grown back on it since, so it's a brown road of hoofprints nobody made on purpose.

areas.name: The Scar
areas.text: A wide band of bare broken earth cutting through the tall grass, hoof marks pressed deep into it.

locations.name: Star Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A round white platform standing on nothing out past the last of the Scattered Isles, gold spires on its towers and a blue star set in its floor. The merfolk say it came up out of the sea one night and the sea never closed over it again. Smugglers row out to it at low tide to scratch their names on the rail, because a name scratched there is supposed to mean you never drown, and some of the names are very old.

areas.name: The Name Rail
areas.text: The white rail along the platform's edge, scratched all over with names.

areas.name: The Spire Towers
areas.text: The little towers round the platform's edge, a gold spire on each, gulls nesting under the points.

areas.name: The Star Floor
areas.text: The blue star set in the middle of the platform, cold underfoot even in the sun.

locations.name: Stillbarrow
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 20-34 · Danger: Severe · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A town of the dead in the grey hills, dug into the old barrows: skeletons keeping shop, ghouls running the bone trade, golems at the gates. It's quiet, it's orderly, and the living who come here keep their voices down.

areas.name: Bell Barrow
areas.text: A barrow with a cracked bell hung over it, rung once when someone new joins the town.

areas.name: Bone Market
areas.text:
A sunken square of old barrows turned into stalls, bones sorted by size, buyers speaking in whispers.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Delvers' Rest (about 3 Iron Ingot), Stiltscale (about 3 Iron Ingot), Cinderforge (about 3 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

areas.name: Bone Stair
areas.text: A stair of fitted bones down into the deepest barrows, swept clean every night.

areas.name: Coffin Row
areas.text: A street of workshops where the skeletons make coffins for anyone who'll pay, measuring you up whether you asked or not.

areas.name: Crypt Rows
areas.text: Streets of open crypts where the town's dead live, lamps burning in the doorways.

areas.name: Embalmers' House
areas.text: A barrow where the newly dead are prepared and the living can pay to be ready.

areas.name: Golem Works
areas.text: A barrow hall full of half-built golems, clay and stone and iron limbs hung from the ceiling.

areas.name: Grave Gardens
areas.text: Rows of grey flowers grown over the graves of the ones who chose to stay dead.

areas.name: Lamp Street
areas.text: The town's main street of barrow doors, a lamp lit at every one and nobody shouting.

areas.name: Mourners' Gate
areas.text: The gate into town, golems standing either side, where the living are told the rules.

areas.name: Quiet Hall
areas.text: The council's hall inside the biggest barrow, cold and silent, with stone seats round a long table.

areas.name: Waking Room
areas.text: A cold stone room where the town's new dead are laid out to get up, and the oldest skeleton in town is there to tell them how it works.

locations.name: Stiltscale
locations.info:
[Town Core · Recommended Level: 10-24 · Danger: High · No major hostile encounters within the settlement itself; surrounding ground remains dangerous]

A lizardfolk town built on stilts over the black water, huts joined by rope walks, boats tied under every floor. It smells of fish and peat smoke and there's always something big moving under the walkways.

areas.name: Boat Moorings
areas.text: Boats tied under the town's floors, reed and hide, knocking against the stilts.

areas.name: Chief's Lodge
areas.text: The biggest hut, built on the thickest stilts, hung with old skulls and dried hydra heads.

areas.name: Croc Pens
areas.text: Fenced channels under the town where the big crocodiles are fed and kept.

areas.name: Eel Traps
areas.text: Wicker traps sunk along the channels, checked at dawn by the young ones.

areas.name: Hatchery
areas.text: A warm, steamy hut over a peat fire where the town's eggs are kept, guarded day and night.

areas.name: Mud Baths
areas.text: A ring of warm mud pools under the huts where the lizardfolk lie in the heat all afternoon and do business with their eyes shut.

areas.name: Net Shed
areas.text: A long shed on stilts hung with nets and floats, the old lizardfolk mending them and telling anyone who'll listen about the big one.

areas.name: Peat Stacks
areas.text: Platforms piled high with cut peat drying for the fires.

areas.name: Reed Shrine
areas.text: A small shrine of bundled reeds over the water, offerings of fish heads left for whatever lives below.

areas.name: Rope Walks
areas.text: Rope walkways strung between the huts on stilts, swaying over the black water.

areas.name: Smoke Huts
areas.text: Huts where fish and eel hang in peat smoke until they'll keep for a season.

areas.name: Stilt Market
areas.text:
A wide platform over the water where boats pull up to sell fish, peat and reeds.

The beetle caravan serves this yard: caravans run to Delvers' Rest (about 3 Iron Ingot), Stillbarrow (about 3 Iron Ingot); ask the caravan master, pay the fare in goods or an ingot, and climb up on the beetle's load.

locations.name: Stonegaze Hollow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 16-18 · Danger: Moderate]

A basilisk's floor, and it shows: grey shapes in every corner that were monsters once, a crowd of stone frozen mid-step. The basilisk sleeps most of the day. You find out it's awake when your feet stop moving.

areas.name: Basilisk Bed
areas.text: A sunken hollow of crushed stone where the basilisk coils to sleep.

areas.name: Mirror Shards
areas.text: A side cave scattered with broken mirror, everything adventurers ever brought to fight the basilisk, all of it smashed.

areas.name: Petrified Pass
areas.text: A narrow pass lined with stone monsters, faces turned toward one end.

areas.name: Stone Crowd
areas.text: A hall packed shoulder to shoulder with statues, as if a whole warband froze together.

locations.name: Strangler Tree
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A huge tree grown round an old stone tower until the tower is just bones inside it, roots and trunk wrapped round every wall, and you climb up through the inside of it to the top.

areas.name: Root Walls
areas.text: A giant tree trunk wrapped round the ruins of a stone tower, roots squeezing through broken windows.

locations.name: Sun Bones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

The bones of something huge half buried in the red sand, ribs high enough to shade a whole caravan, where everyone crossing the waste stops to sit out the noon sun.

areas.name: Rib Shade
areas.text: The shade under the great ribs, the sand cool and packed flat by everyone who's sat out the noon here.

locations.name: Sunk Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: Moderate]

An old human road that runs straight into the fen and under the black water, the paving still there a foot down, the only solid footing for a mile in any direction.

areas.name: Road's End
areas.text: Where the road goes under, the last dry paving stones and then black water with the road showing pale beneath it.

locations.name: Sunken Temple
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A temple of green stone half swallowed by the jungle, roots through every wall, steps going down into water. Something built it before the humans and before the monsters, and the lizardfolk who live round it won't go past the third step.

areas.name: Flooded Nave
areas.text: The temple's hall, half under black water, carvings of things with too many arms on every wall.

areas.name: Idol Chamber
areas.text: A small dark room at the top with one great stone idol, its eyes worn smooth by hands.

areas.name: Temple Steps
areas.text: Wide green steps going up out of the jungle to the temple, vines thick as arms across them.

locations.name: Temple Stone
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-40 · Danger: Severe]

A standing stone on the way to the Sunken Temple, carved with the same shape as the temple door. The lizardfolk say the stone is the key and the temple is the lock, and they won't touch either.

areas.name: Door Carving
areas.text: The carving on the stone, the same shape as the temple door.

locations.name: Terrace Dig
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

Stepped terraces cut into a hill of brown rock under the snow, where the frost ogres dig iron, the only bare ground for miles because the hill is warm. The ogres won't say why it's warm and they won't let anyone dig the bottom terrace.

areas.name: Bottom Terrace
areas.text: The lowest terrace, roped off, the rock there warm to the hand.

locations.name: The Amber Marsh
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A marsh of glowing amber water in the north west of the dome, warm as a bath, with clumps of reeds standing in it and a round green pavilion on stilts out in the middle reached by raised walkways. The mandrakes grow in the shallows with only their leaves showing, and the amber light comes off the water so strong that the whole corner glows gold at night. Pull a mandrake up and it screams, and the scream takes your breath for a day.

areas.name: The Glowing Water
areas.text: The warm amber marsh water.

areas.name: The Reed Beds
areas.text: The clumps of reeds where the mandrakes grow.

areas.name: The Stilt Pavilion
areas.text: The round green pavilion on stilts in the middle of the marsh.

locations.name: The Armillary
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A great round platform standing in the star-sea with a gold armillary sphere in the middle of it, rings inside rings turning slowly round a white pearl that glows like the moon. The gazers built it to read the sky, and they read it all day and all night, the big ones floating at the rings and the little ones zipping between them calling out what they see. Every road and bridge in the dome comes back here. If you want to know something, ask the gazers, and if you don't want to know what's coming, don't stand where the pearl's light falls on you.

areas.name: The Blue Floor
areas.text: The round blue platform under the sphere, gold lines and stars set into it like a chart.

areas.name: The Sphere
areas.text: The gold rings and the glowing pearl at the centre, turning.

areas.name: The Stair Down
areas.text: The white stair from the platform down to the bridge that runs south to the Black Well.

locations.name: The Black Well
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A hole in the star-sea where the water spins round and round and down into a black centre with a ring of violet light round it, and the rock around it broken into jagged grey teeth. A long bridge on gold chains crosses over it from the Armillary, with flat stones hanging off the chains under it, and the stars in the water all lean towards the hole. The gazers won't look into it. The merfolk keep the rest of the sea and leave this part alone.

areas.name: The Black Centre
areas.text: The hole itself, the violet ring round it, the water going down.

areas.name: The Chain Bridge
areas.text: The long bridge hanging over the well on gold chains.

areas.name: The Hanging Plates
areas.text: The flat stones swinging on chains under the bridge.

locations.name: The Brass Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 33-35 · Danger: Severe]

Somebody built these halls and it wasn't monsters: doors of brass, a floor of anvils, bellows taller than a troll still pumping on their own. The heat comes from the forges, and the forges have no fire in them.

areas.name: Anvil Floor
areas.text: A hall whose floor is made of anvils set side by side, ringing when you walk.

areas.name: Bellows Hall
areas.text: Giant leather bellows rising and falling on their own, blowing hot air through the floor.

areas.name: Brass Doors
areas.text: Tall doors of tarnished brass covered in shapes of chains and flames.

areas.name: Maker's Bench
areas.text: A workbench of brass and tools left mid-job, a half-built thing on it that ticks if you stand close.

locations.name: The Chained Rocks
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Three flat slabs of rock floating in the open violet air past the Scales, cracked through with gold light and hung from the dome on gold chains with rings at the top, swinging a little whenever the Scales tip. Prisoners are kept on them, things the Seal caught and didn't know what to do with, one to a rock and the chain too short to jump. Getting out to them means flying, or getting a sylph to carry you, and the sylphs want something for it.

areas.name: The Empty Rock
areas.text: The far slab, swept clean, its chain new.

areas.name: The First Rock
areas.text: The nearest slab, low and close enough to the cliff edge to shout across to.

areas.name: The Hanging Chains
areas.text: The gold chains and rings the rocks hang from, running up into the dark of the dome.

locations.name: The Coaching Inn
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human coaching inn on the old road west, the stables empty and the beds still made, the dust on the bar thick enough to write in.

areas.name: Taproom
areas.text: The inn's taproom, chairs up on the tables, the bar thick with dust and the list of names written in it.

locations.name: The Crystal Cliffs
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Grey cliffs along the dome's east wall with violet crystal growing out of the rock in clumps and violet light running down the cracks like water, and little round stones floating off the cliff face on short gold chains. The pixies come here to break off crystal for their lights, and the crystal grows back by the next night. Anything that falls off these cliffs falls into the star-sea, and the merfolk don't fish it out.

areas.name: The Crystal Clumps
areas.text: The violet crystal pushing out of the grey rock.

areas.name: The Floating Stones
areas.text: The round stones hanging off the cliffs on short gold chains.

areas.name: The Lit Cracks
areas.text: The violet light running down the cliff face.

locations.name: The Crystal Ridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A broken ridge of purple rock along the Seal's north west wall, with gold crystal growing out of the cracks in clumps taller than an ogre and a lone round shrine at the top of a cliff that nothing has a road to. The crystal is what the golems are made of, and when one breaks the others come up here and grow a new one out of the ridge, which takes a season and makes a noise like a bell the whole time. The gargoyles on the north west obelisk watch the ridge and drive off anything that picks at the crystal.

areas.name: The Crystal Spikes
areas.text: The clumps of gold crystal pushing out of the rock, warm, humming when you get close.

areas.name: The Lone Shrine
areas.text: The small round shrine alone on its cliff top, no path up.

areas.name: The North West Obelisk
areas.text: The sun obelisk on the wall above the ridge, gargoyles all over it.

locations.name: The Dead Trees
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Grey ground in the south west of the prison with a few great white trees standing dead on it, branches like bones, and broken standing stones scattered round them. The shades gather here, thin grey shapes standing still among the trees, and they don't do anything, they just stand there facing the Pit. The imps say the trees were alive when the prison was built.

areas.name: The Bone Trees
areas.text: The dead white trees with branches like bones.

areas.name: The Broken Stones
areas.text: The cracked standing stones among the trees.

areas.name: The Shade Ground
areas.text: The bare grey ground where the shades stand facing the Pit.

locations.name: The Dead Wood
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The west side of the dome where nothing is green: great white trees lying fallen and hollow on dry brown ground, a dark stream winding between them and mushrooms growing off the logs as big as tables. It's where the Covenant puts what it's finished with, and the myconids live in it and eat it down slowly. The air smells like wet bark and the myconids talk to each other in puffs of spores.

areas.name: The Dark Stream
areas.text: The black stream winding through the dead wood.

areas.name: The Hollow Logs
areas.text: The fallen white trees lying open and hollow.

areas.name: The Table Mushrooms
areas.text: The huge flat mushrooms growing off the logs.

locations.name: The Drip
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 1-3 · Danger: Low]

Water comes through the ceiling all over this floor, one drop at a time, and where it lands it eats. Boots go soft, rope goes rotten and the goblins up top pay good scrap for anyone willing to carry buckets of it out, because it cleans a bone better than anything in the Basin.

areas.name: Bucket Line
areas.text: A path of planks the goblins laid between the dry spots, buckets stacked at one end.

areas.name: Drip Hall
areas.text: A long hall ticking with drops from the ceiling, every one leaving a pale pock in the stone.

areas.name: Lime Pools
areas.text: Shallow white pools of collected drip that fizz when you drop something in.

areas.name: Rust Room
areas.text: A small room where everything metal that came down the Drip ended up, a heap of red rust that used to be swords.

locations.name: The Drowned Market
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 28-30 · Danger: High]

A whole human market sank down here somehow, stalls and carts and a fountain, and the merfolk pick it over with nets. Everything is under a few feet of black water and covered in silt, and some of it is still for sale.

areas.name: Bubble Bell
areas.text: An iron bell hung upside down full of trapped air, where the merfolk trade with air-breathers.

areas.name: Net Lofts
areas.text: An old market building half out of the water where the merfolk hang their nets and sort the day's finds.

areas.name: Silt Floor
areas.text: A floor of deep soft silt that clouds the water black at one step.

areas.name: Sunk Stalls
areas.text: Rows of drowned market stalls, awnings rotting, goods silted over under black water.

locations.name: The Echo Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 9-11 · Danger: Low]

Every sound on this floor comes back three times, louder, and from the wrong direction. Hunters love it because their prey runs the wrong way; everything else hates it because you never know what's actually behind you.

areas.name: Echo Gallery
areas.text: A long curved gallery where a footstep comes back as a crowd.

areas.name: Hunters' Blind
areas.text: A low dead-end room where the echoes don't reach, the hunters' best spot to sit and listen for whatever's running.

areas.name: Quiet Nook
areas.text: A small dead room padded with moss where sound goes nowhere, the only rest on the floor.

areas.name: Whisper Stair
areas.text: A spiral stair where anything said at the top is heard clearly at the bottom.

locations.name: The Empty Capital
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The humans' capital, past the Iron March: walls, towers, streets of stone houses, a palace on the hill, all of it standing and empty, doors open, washing still on the lines. Monsters who go in come out quiet.

areas.name: King's Road
areas.text: The main street up to the palace, shops still stocked, nobody behind the counters.

areas.name: Throne Hall
areas.text: The palace's great hall, the throne empty, a map of the Wildreach on the wall with every town marked.

areas.name: West Gate
areas.text: The great gate through the city's eastern wall, its doors open, the road running in.

locations.name: The Falling Pools
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Two pools of bright blue water on two steps of rock with a waterfall pouring from one into the next, and round domed shrines on stone posts standing in and around them. The water comes out of the rock above and goes nowhere, falling from pool to pool and back up again when nobody is looking. The golems wash their cracks in it to keep the gold bright, and anything wounded that gets in the water comes out healed, which is why the golems don't let anything but golems in it.

areas.name: The Low Pool
areas.text: The big lower pool behind the wall, gold light lying on the water in lines.

areas.name: The Pool Shrines
areas.text: The domed stone shrines on their posts round the water, each with a golem standing inside.

areas.name: The Top Pool
areas.text: The upper pool under the cliff, the falls coming out of the rock above it.

locations.name: The First Keeper's Hold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 11-12 · Danger: Low]

The bottom of the Upper Halls, where the dungeon put its first real guard. The halls get narrow, the moss goes out and the floor is polished smooth by everything that walked this far and stopped. Most monsters turn round here and they aren't ashamed of it.

areas.name: First Keeper's Door
areas.text: A great stone door at the bottom of the Upper Halls, where the floor's keeper waits.

areas.name: Keeper's Approach
areas.text: A long narrowing hall, its walls scored with claw marks at every height.

areas.name: Keeper's Den
areas.text: The keeper's room behind the door, littered with the gear of everything that lost.

areas.name: Trophy Wall
areas.text: A wall by the keeper's door hung with the weapons of everything that came to fight it, the newest still bloody.

locations.name: The Furnace
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 37-39 · Danger: Severe]

The fire road's heart, a furnace bigger than Delvers' Rest, its mouth open and roaring. Nothing lives here long, and the things that do are made of fire themselves.

areas.name: Clinker Heaps
areas.text: Heaps of burnt-out slag and bone raked out of the furnace, still smoking.

areas.name: Draft Tunnels
areas.text: Tunnels where the furnace sucks air in with a howl, pulling at everything.

areas.name: Furnace Mouth
areas.text: The roaring open mouth of the great furnace, white-hot inside.

areas.name: Stoker's Ledge
areas.text: A ledge by the furnace mouth where the imps throw in the fuel, and the fuel is whatever they caught this week.

locations.name: The Gate of Fire
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 39-40 · Danger: Severe]

The bottom of the fire road: a gate of black iron in a wall of flame, shut, with something on the other side pushing. The imps have built a little town of shacks round it so they can watch.

areas.name: Cooling Room
areas.text: A side room where the imps who guard the gate come to cool off, buckets of water and a lot of steam.

areas.name: Fire Gate
areas.text: A gate of black iron set in a wall of fire, bowed outward as if pushed from behind.

areas.name: Gatewatch
areas.text: Imp shacks built up against the heat, every one with a window facing the gate.

areas.name: Scorched Threshold
areas.text: The black ground before the gate, cracked and glassy, nothing left standing on it.

locations.name: The Gnawed Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 7-9 · Danger: Low]

The floor stops at a chasm and one stone bridge crosses it, chewed thin in the middle by something nobody has seen. Bats hang under it in their thousands and the drop goes further than any rock you throw.

areas.name: Bat Cliffs
areas.text: The chasm walls under the bridge, black and moving with bats.

areas.name: Chasm Lip
areas.text: The edge of the floor where it drops away, ropes and pitons left by the ones who tried to climb.

areas.name: Gnawed Bridge
areas.text: A stone bridge over the chasm, bitten down to a hand's width at its middle.

areas.name: Gnawer's Hole
areas.text: A round hole in the chasm wall under the bridge, chewed clean, the floor of it covered in stone dust and teeth.

locations.name: The Gold Grove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A spread of white-barked trees with gold leaves on yellow grass, the only living green in the Seal, and the sylphs' home. They sleep in the canopy and sing the trees up when they need more. A paved path winds through it from the gate to the Scales, and anything that steps off the path gets the sylphs coming down out of the branches to ask why. The leaves fall gold and stay gold, and a golem walks the grove every evening picking every one of them up.

areas.name: The Grove Path
areas.text: The paved path winding through the grove from the Sun Gate to the Scales.

areas.name: The Leaf Fall
areas.text: The low ground at the grove's south edge where the gold leaves drift and pile before the golem gets to them.

areas.name: The White Trees
areas.text: The biggest of the trees, their roots coming up through the grass like knuckles, the sylphs' nests up top.

locations.name: The Great Trees
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Huge flat-topped trees in the north east of the dome with green halls built into their roots and terraces stepping down between them. The dryads live in the trees and come out of the trunks when they want to talk. The halls are where the Covenant keeps the promises it made, one carved into every wall, the oldest ones grown over with bark.

areas.name: The Promise Walls
areas.text: The hall walls with the promises carved into them, the old ones grown over.

areas.name: The Root Halls
areas.text: The long green halls built into the roots of the trees.

areas.name: The Tree Terraces
areas.text: The steps of terrace stepping down between the trees.

locations.name: The Green Door
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A green stone archway where the Rootway comes into the dome, roots wrapped round its frame and a long stair running straight down from it into the middle of the Covenant. A treant stands either side of it, so still and so overgrown they look like part of the wall until they move. They ask what you've brought to give, because nothing comes into the Covenant without giving something to it, and nothing goes out without being given something back.

areas.name: The Door Treants
areas.text: The two treants standing either side, moss on their shoulders.

areas.name: The Long Stair Down
areas.text: The straight stair running from the door down into the Covenant.

areas.name: The Root Frame
areas.text: The green stone arch with the roots wrapped round its frame.

locations.name: The Gullet
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 44-46 · Danger: Deadly]

A long ribbed slope going down, wet and warm, with pools of bile that burn through iron. Anything that falls here keeps sliding until something catches it, and something always does.

areas.name: Bile Pools
areas.text: Pools of yellow-green bile smoking where they touch the stone.

areas.name: Catch Basin
areas.text: A pool at the bottom of the slope where everything that slid down the Gullet stops, and the bile in it is waist deep.

areas.name: Gullet Slope
areas.text: A steep wet slope of ribbed red stone going down into the dark.

areas.name: Ribbed Hall
areas.text: A round hall ringed with ridges like the inside of a throat.

locations.name: The Hanging Cells
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Chunks of rock hung on thick gold chains over a pit of violet fire in the north east, swinging slowly, with a cell cut into the top of each one. The prisoners on them are the ones the imps want to hear, because they scream when the rock swings low over the fire, and the imps like to know things. A troll works the big winch at the edge that lowers and raises them.

areas.name: The Fire Below
areas.text: The violet fire under the rocks, crackling up when one swings low.

areas.name: The Swinging Rocks
areas.text: The rocks on their chains, a cell cut in the top of each.

areas.name: The Winch
areas.text: The big troll-worked winch at the cliff edge that moves the chains.

locations.name: The Heart
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 49-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The bottom of the Great Dungeon. The walls are warm and soft and they move, slow, like something breathing.

areas.name: Feeding Floor
areas.text: The floor round the well, worn smooth, scattered with what's left of everything that reached the bottom.

areas.name: Heart Chamber
areas.text: A round chamber of warm red stone that rises and falls, a glow pulsing somewhere behind the walls.

areas.name: Last Step
areas.text: The last step before the Soul Well, worn smooth, and everything that ever made it this far stood here first.

areas.name: Soul Well
areas.text: A pit in the floor full of slow pale light, souls drifting in it.

locations.name: The Heart Seed
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

At the bottom of the Covenant, wrapped in a cradle of roots as tall as a tower, a great seed burns gold and orange like a fire in a fist, with a stair running down to it and green halls round the base. Everything in the Covenant grows from it. The treants guard it in shifts, and the roots of every tree in the world end up here eventually, the dryads say, and that's how the Covenant knows what happens everywhere.

areas.name: The Burning Seed
areas.text: The gold and orange seed glowing in the cradle.

areas.name: The Root Cradle
areas.text: The tower of roots wrapped round the seed.

areas.name: The Seed Stair
areas.text: The stair running down from the halls to the seed.

locations.name: The Hungry Chests
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 23-25 · Danger: High]

The mimics of the Upper Halls are the runts. The ones down here are the size of a cart, stacked up a cliff like a city of boxes, and their tongues reach across the hall. They talk to each other in creaks.

areas.name: Chest Cliff
areas.text: A cliff face built of stacked chests, some breathing, lids cracked open on rows of teeth.

areas.name: Empty Lids
areas.text: A ledge of dead mimics, lids hanging open and teeth gone grey, where the big ones drag the ones they've beaten.

areas.name: Mimic Mother
areas.text: A chest as big as a house at the top of the cliff, its lid carved like a crown.

areas.name: Tongue Bridge
areas.text: A bridge across a gap that is really one long grey tongue, warm and slick.

locations.name: The Labyrinth
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-17 · Danger: Moderate]

A maze that rebuilds itself every night, walls grinding into new places while you sleep. The minotaurs down here were born in it and always know the way, and they charge a toll in meat to lead you through.

areas.name: Calf Pens
areas.text: A walled dead end where the minotaur young are kept, butting the walls and each other until they're big enough for the maze.

areas.name: Horn Hall
areas.text: A round hall hung with broken horns where the minotaurs meet and bargain.

areas.name: Maze Gate
areas.text: The way in: two horned pillars and a floor scraped smooth by hooves.

areas.name: Wrong Turn
areas.text: A dead end full of bones of the ones who thought they knew the way.

locations.name: The Lantern Run
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 10-12 · Danger: Low]

Lanterns the adventurers hung a lifetime ago are still burning down this floor and nobody has ever seen them refilled. The walls are scratched all over with their maps, arrows and warnings, most of them still right.

areas.name: Lantern Row
areas.text: A long hall of iron lanterns on hooks, each burning a steady pale yellow.

areas.name: Last Lantern
areas.text: A small room at the end of the run with one lantern still burning on a hook and nobody's ever found what it burns.

areas.name: Map Wall
areas.text: A wall cut over with old maps of the floors, arrows, crosses and the word 'down' again and again.

areas.name: Oil Pits
areas.text: Clay jars sunk in the floor full of thick oil that never runs dry.

locations.name: The Last Keepers
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 47-49 · Danger: Deadly]

The dungeon keeps its oldest keepers here, the ones too strong to send up, sitting on thrones of their own bones, waiting. Each one guards a step down.

areas.name: Broken Crowns
areas.text: A pile of crowns, helms and horns taken from kings that came down and stayed.

areas.name: Empty Throne
areas.text: A throne of bones with nobody on it, the one keeper who left, and the others watch it all the time.

areas.name: Heart Gate
areas.text: A gate of ribs closing off the way down, opening only for whoever beats the row.

areas.name: Keepers' Row
areas.text: A long hall of bone thrones, a huge shape sitting in each.

locations.name: The Leaf Circle
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A round green lawn in the middle of the Covenant with a great tree drawn into the grass and the roots of the whole place braiding together across it in thick cords, every road in the dome meeting here. This is where the Covenant makes its promises, the treants standing in a ring round the lawn and the roots moving under it as they talk. A promise made in the circle grows. A promise broken in the circle grows too, the other way, and it doesn't stop.

areas.name: The Braided Roots
areas.text: The thick roots braiding together across the lawn.

areas.name: The Drawn Tree
areas.text: The tree shape in the grass at the centre of the circle.

areas.name: The Treant Ring
areas.text: Where the treants stand when they meet.

locations.name: The Lightless Lake
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 32-34 · Danger: Severe]

A flooded cavern so big the water looks like the sky at night, black and still, no far shore anyone has reached. Light doesn't go far here; a torch shows you the water and nothing else.

areas.name: Black Island
areas.text: A hump of black rock rising from the lake, a single lit window in a ruin on top.

areas.name: Cold Current
areas.text: A channel where the lake runs fast and freezing toward a crack in the wall.

areas.name: Lake Edge
areas.text: A narrow rock shore along black water that runs flat into the dark.

areas.name: Lamp Wreck
areas.text: A wrecked boat on the lake shore with a lamp still on its bow, the only light on the lake and nothing ever goes near it.

locations.name: The Lightning Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A straight stone road from the gatehouse to the dome with gold rings set in its floor and violet lightning crackling up both sides of it the whole way, never touching the road but never stopping either. The imps say it keeps things in, not out. Walk down the middle and you're fine. Step to the edge and the lightning finds you, and the hellhounds at the far end come running when they hear somebody scream.

areas.name: The Lightning Sides
areas.text: The violet lightning crackling up along both edges of the road.

areas.name: The Post Stones
areas.text: The square stone posts along the road's sides, each one burnt black on top.

areas.name: The Ring Floor
areas.text: The gold rings set in a line down the middle of the road, the safe way across.

locations.name: The Lit Door
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A great arched opening cut into the cliff on the west side, glowing orange from inside like a forge, with tiered stone galleries built round it and a long stair running down to the yard. It's where the imps work, making new locks and new chains and new keys, and the noise of the hammers comes out of it day and night. The trolls carry the iron in. The shades won't go near the light.

areas.name: The Forge Stair
areas.text: The long stair from the arch down to the yard.

areas.name: The Galleries
areas.text: The tiered stone galleries built round the arch, imps running along them.

areas.name: The Glowing Arch
areas.text: The huge orange-lit opening in the cliff.

locations.name: The Lotus Falls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Turquoise water falling down the east side of the dome in a stair of falls, pool to pool, with green pavilions on every terrace and white lotus flowers on the pools as big as a cart. The dryads come down here to bathe and the treants send the wounded here. A lotus opens for anything that lies on it hurt and closes over it, and when it opens again in the morning the wound is gone.

areas.name: The Falls Stair
areas.text: The falls running down the east side from pool to pool.

areas.name: The Lotus Pools
areas.text: The pools with the huge white lotus flowers on them.

areas.name: The Terrace Pavilions
areas.text: The green roofed pavilions on each terrace.

locations.name: The Mantis Grove
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-22 · Danger: Moderate]

Crystal grows out of the floor here like reeds, taller than an ogre, and the mantids stand in it so still you walk right past them. The crystal sings when the wind from below comes up, and that's when they move.

areas.name: Ambush Reeds
areas.text: A thick stand of crystal reeds where the mantids wait, so still the only way to tell them apart is that the reeds don't breathe.

areas.name: Crystal Reeds
areas.text: A forest of thin crystal spikes taller than an ogre, ringing softly.

areas.name: Molt Hollow
areas.text: A hollow full of shed mantis skins, perfect and empty, standing up like they're still inside.

areas.name: Praying Stones
areas.text: A clearing of flat rocks where the mantids stand with their arms folded, waiting.

locations.name: The Meeting Pool
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 40-42 · Danger: Severe]

Where the fire road and the water road meet again: a cavern full of steam, a pool in the middle boiling where the two pour in together. Below this, everything is the Heart.

areas.name: Meeting Pool
areas.text: A round pool boiling where a stream of fire and a stream of water fall into it together.

areas.name: Mixing Shelf
areas.text: A shelf of rock over the pool where the fire and the water meet in a hiss, the steam so thick you walk it by feel.

areas.name: Steam Gallery
areas.text: A gallery wrapped in hot white steam, water dripping from every surface.

areas.name: Twin Stairs
areas.text: Two stairs coming down into the cavern from opposite sides, one black with soot, one green with weed.

locations.name: The Middle Keeper's Hold
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 24-25 · Danger: High]

The bottom of the Middle Depths, the second guard post. The air gets warm and wet like breath and the floor slopes down toward a door of black stone. Below it the dungeon splits in two, and nothing that goes through comes back the same.

areas.name: Black Stair
areas.text: A wide stair of black stone going down, warm to the touch and damp.

areas.name: Keeper's Bones
areas.text: A hall heaped with the bones of earlier keepers, fire-black on one side and drowned green on the other.

areas.name: Middle Keeper's Door
areas.text: A door of black stone at the bottom of the Middle Depths, warm to the touch.

areas.name: Toll Post
areas.text: A guard post on the stair down with a stone bowl where the smart ones leave something for the keeper and walk past.

locations.name: The Millhouse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human mill on a stream with its wheel still turning, a stone house, barns and fields, good walls and good ground for anyone bold enough to move into a human's home.

areas.name: Mill Wheel
areas.text: A stone mill on a quick stream, its wheel still turning, empty fields gone to seed all round.

locations.name: The Moon Orrery
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A gold crescent moon as tall as a tower standing on a round terrace with an orrery set in its curve, gold rings and a ball turning for the moon's phases, and a long white stair coming down from it to the cliffs below. The gazers come up here to read the moon on its own, and on the night it's full the merfolk come up the stair out of the water to stand under it in silence. What the orrery shows the gazers don't say, but they've been watching it more lately.

areas.name: The Crescent
areas.text: The huge gold crescent moon, cold to touch.

areas.name: The Moon Rings
areas.text: The gold orrery inside the crescent, turning slowly.

areas.name: The Moon Stair
areas.text: The wide white stair from the moon's terrace down to the east cliffs.

locations.name: The Mossway
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 3-5 · Danger: Low]

The glowing moss grows thickest here, a blue-green carpet up the walls and over the ceiling, and the myconids farm it in neat beds. It's the quietest floor in the Upper Halls and the only one where things don't try to eat you on sight.

areas.name: Farm Terraces
areas.text: Steps of moss beds cut into the wall, the myconids tending each one, the glow brightest where the crop is ripe.

areas.name: Glow Pool
areas.text: A still pool lit from underneath by moss on its bed, clean enough to drink.

areas.name: Moss Beds
areas.text: Long raised beds of glowing moss tended in rows, the light soft and steady.

areas.name: Spore Pantry
areas.text: A dry cave of hanging mushrooms drying on strings, the air thick and sweet.

locations.name: The Ossuary
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 5-7 · Danger: Low]

The dungeon keeps the bones of every adventurer it ever ate on this floor, stacked in neat shelves like somebody's pantry, and some nights the shelves get up and walk. The skeletons down here still wear what they died in.

areas.name: Last Bunks
areas.text: A barracks room of stone bunks with a skeleton laid in each, some still holding their swords.

areas.name: Rattling Rows
areas.text: Aisles between the shelves where the bones click and shift when nobody's looking.

areas.name: Skull Shelves
areas.text: Walls of carved shelves stacked with skulls, every one facing the same way.

areas.name: Sorting Nook
areas.text: A nook where the bones are sorted before they go on the shelves, skulls in one pile, hands in another, and something does the sorting at night.

locations.name: The Pit
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A great round paved yard in the middle of the prison with a ring wall round it and a deep round pit in its centre, four stairs going down into it from the four sides and a slow violet swirl at the bottom you can't see past. Whatever the prison was built for is down there. The four stairs only go halfway down, the gold rings set round the yard's floor glow brighter every night, and the trolls who sweep the yard won't go near the edge.

areas.name: The Half Stairs
areas.text: The four stairs going down into the pit that stop halfway.

areas.name: The Ring Yard
areas.text: The round paved yard round the pit, gold rings set in the floor.

areas.name: The Swirl Below
areas.text: The violet swirl at the bottom of the pit.

locations.name: The Pulse
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 48-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The beat is loud enough here to shake your teeth, the walls red and wet and pushing in time, everything moving with it. You walk between beats or you get thrown.

areas.name: Beat Stair
areas.text: A stair that jolts with every beat, steps slick with red.

areas.name: Pulse Hall
areas.text: A hall of red walls that swell and shrink in time with a deep beat.

areas.name: Red Halls
areas.text: Narrow halls the colour of raw meat, warm wind pushing through them on the beat.

areas.name: Valve Gate
areas.text: A wet red gate in the wall that opens and shuts with the beat, and you go through it between beats or not at all.

locations.name: The Ribcage
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-47 · Danger: Deadly]

A floor built inside a ribcage, each rib as tall as a tower, curving up into the dark overhead. Whatever owned these bones was bigger than anything alive, and the dungeon grew in it.

areas.name: Bone Bridge
areas.text: A bridge of a single giant bone across a gap, worn smooth by feet.

areas.name: Marrow Cracks
areas.text: Cracks in a huge bone, glowing faintly with old marrow.

areas.name: Rib Gallery
areas.text: A gallery between two giant curving ribs, the bone yellow and pitted.

areas.name: Spine Walk
areas.text: A path along the top of the great spine, the ribs curving away either side, a long way down if you slip.

locations.name: The Root Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A round green stone arch at the bottom edge of the Deepgreen with a swirl of amber light in it, roots as thick as an ogre wrapped round it on both sides holding it up out of the ground, little stone towers on its shoulders. The jungle's lizardfolk say the roots pulled it up out of the ground the way a tree pulls up a stone, and every year the roots are a little thicker. Walk into the amber and you're on the Rootway, and the roots close behind you.

areas.name: The Amber Arch
areas.text: The round green arch with the swirl of amber light in it.

areas.name: The Holding Roots
areas.text: The huge roots wrapped round the arch from both sides.

areas.name: The Shoulder Towers
areas.text: The little green stone towers on the arch's shoulders, moss on every ledge.

locations.name: The Root Road
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A green stone road running down from the gate with gold lines in its floor like veins in a leaf, two rings of amber light across it where the stone breaks off, and roots coming up from below gripping both sides of it the whole way down. Cross a ring and the road carries on below it. The treants' roots move when nobody's looking, and the way the road bends today is not the way it bent yesterday.

areas.name: The Amber Rings
areas.text: The two rings of amber light where the road breaks off.

areas.name: The Gripping Roots
areas.text: The roots holding the road on both sides.

areas.name: The Leaf Floor
areas.text: The green stone road with gold veins running through it.

locations.name: The Round Seats
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A half-ring of stone seats built down a slope on its own island, facing a round stage with a blue star in it, lilac trees and crystal round the edges. The sirens sing here for anyone who'll listen, and the pixies do plays about things the gazers have seen coming, with themselves in all the parts, and a monster who sits through a whole play gets a pixie's light to keep. Nobody knows what happens to the ones who leave halfway.

areas.name: The Lilac Trees
areas.text: The pale purple trees round the seats where the pixies sleep.

areas.name: The Star Stage
areas.text: The round stage at the bottom of the seats, the blue star in its floor.

areas.name: The Stone Seats
areas.text: The rows of curved seats going up the slope.

locations.name: The Scales
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The heart of the Seal, a great round paved plaza with a gold sun cut into the floor and a pair of scales inside it, and a ring of arched stone walls around the edge like the seats of a court. This is where every soul in the world gets weighed when its body dies, set on the scales where nobody living can see it and sent on down into the Swirl or up the Sun Stair, and the golems stand round the walls all day and all night watching scales that never stop moving. The roads in from every part of the Seal all come here.

areas.name: The Court Arches
areas.text: The ring of arched walls round the plaza, a golem standing in every arch.

areas.name: The Four Roads
areas.text: Where the paths from the gate, the stair, the grove and the Swirl meet at the plaza's edge.

areas.name: The Scale Floor
areas.text: The gold sun and scales set into the plaza floor, the scale pans swaying with nothing on them you can see.

locations.name: The Shade Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 42-44 · Danger: Deadly]

Shades live here, the ghosts of things the dungeon ate that never made it into the Soul Well, stretched thin and cold. Light gets swallowed and your own shadow goes on ahead of you.

areas.name: Cold Room
areas.text: The coldest room in the halls, where the shades gather thickest, your breath freezing in front of you.

areas.name: Lost Light
areas.text: A hall where torchlight dies a step from the flame, the dark close and cold.

areas.name: Name Wall
areas.text: A wall scratched with thousands of names, some still being added by unseen hands.

areas.name: Shadow Gallery
areas.text: A gallery where shadows move on the walls with nothing to cast them.

locations.name: The Slag Sea
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 29-31 · Danger: High]

A lake of lava as wide as the Basin, crusted black on top with red showing through the cracks. The only way across is rock to floating rock, and the rocks sink if you stand on them too long.

areas.name: Cooling Crust
areas.text: A skin of black crust over the lava that holds, mostly, cracking red at every step.

areas.name: Crust Camp
areas.text: A big flat rock out on the slag where the salamanders camp, cooking on the cracks and laughing at anyone trying to cross.

areas.name: Floating Rocks
areas.text: Rocks bobbing on the lava in a broken line toward the far side, each one slowly sinking.

areas.name: Slag Shore
areas.text: A black shore of cooled slag at the edge of the lava lake, glowing in the seams.

locations.name: The Sluices
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A dark river running down through the south of the prison in steps, with tall stone sluice gates glowing orange between the pools and a waterfall where the river drops a level. The trolls open and shut the gates to fill and empty the lower pools, and the low pool by the south wall is where the prison drowns things it can't keep any other way. The water's black and the light from the gates lies on it in orange stripes.

areas.name: The Drop
areas.text: The waterfall where the river steps down a level.

areas.name: The Drowning Pool
areas.text: The big low pool against the south wall.

areas.name: The Sluice Gates
areas.text: The tall stone gates between the pools, glowing orange through their bars.

locations.name: The Soft Halls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 41-43 · Danger: Deadly]

The stone goes soft on this floor. It gives under your feet, warm, and when you lean on a wall you feel it lean back. Veins run through the floor like roots.

areas.name: Sinking Floor
areas.text: A room where the floor gives under you like mud and closes back up, and things have gone down in it and not come up.

areas.name: Soft Corridor
areas.text: A corridor whose walls give like flesh when touched, warm and faintly moving.

areas.name: Vein Arch
areas.text: An arch of thick red veins over the way down, pulsing slowly.

areas.name: Warm Floor
areas.text: A floor that rises and falls slightly, warm through boots.

locations.name: The Spike Landing
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A squat violet stone gatehouse standing out past the humans' land on nothing, a curved spike on each side of it like a horn and a heavy barred door, and a gold ring cut into the stone over the bars. The humans had a word for it that meant don't, and their old roads all stop a mile short of it. The hellhounds lie on its step in pairs and lift their heads at anything coming. Knock on the bars and an imp comes to see who's stupid enough.

areas.name: The Barred Door
areas.text: The heavy barred door with the gold ring over it, the only thing between the road and the outside.

areas.name: The Horn Spikes
areas.text: The two curved stone spikes either side of the gatehouse, warm, humming in a storm.

areas.name: The Hound Step
areas.text: The wide stone step in front of the door where the hellhounds sleep.

locations.name: The Spinning Dark
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 13-15 · Danger: Moderate]

The arachnes raise their young on this floor and keep it dark on purpose. You walk it by feel through silk that's soft as hair, and the clicking you hear is a hundred mothers deciding whether you're worth the trouble.

areas.name: Egg Sacs
areas.text: Pale sacs the size of barrels hung in clusters from the ceiling, twitching.

areas.name: Hanging Path
areas.text: A walkway of thick webbing over a black drop, the only way across.

areas.name: Silk Loom
areas.text: A hall strung floor to ceiling with sheets of woven silk, swaying in no wind.

areas.name: Wrapped Larder
areas.text: A dark chamber hung with silk-wrapped bundles, the arachnes' larder, and some of the bundles are still moving.

locations.name: The Star Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]
