A long straight bridge from the landing to the dome with nothing under it, blue light running along both sides of it in ribbons, and three blue stars set into its deck one after another. Walk it at night and the stars in the deck light up one by one as you reach them, and the ribbons sing a low note that the sirens inside take up and carry. Nothing flies over it. The gulls go round.

areas.name: The First Star
areas.text: The first blue star in the deck, where the light starts following you.

areas.name: The Last Star
areas.text: The star right before the dome's gate, where the bridge widens out.

areas.name: The Light Ribbons
areas.text: The bands of blue light flowing along both sides of the bridge, humming.

locations.name: The Star Falls
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Pools of bright turquoise water on stepped rock islands under the north wall, falling from one into the next in thin white falls, with domed blue pavilions on the high islands and lilac trees all round. The sirens live in the pools and sing the hours from them, one song for every hour of the night, and the merfolk keep the falls running clear. Over all of it, set in the top of the dome's wall, is the gold compass star that the gazers say points at the real north.

areas.name: The Compass Star
areas.text: The great gold star in the north wall, its points running out over the dome.

areas.name: The Falls Steps
areas.text: The falls running down between the islands into the lower pools.

areas.name: The High Pavilions
areas.text: The domed blue pavilions on the top islands, where the sirens sit to sing.

locations.name: The Star Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A white arch in the dome's wall with a gold star at its point, and inside it a slow swirl of blue light with stars turning in it, which is the only way in. Two gazers float in the arch, one above the other, and look at whoever comes up the bridge for a long time before they let them through. They aren't looking at your face. Gazers read what's coming for you, and they let in the ones whose future they can't see.

areas.name: The Inner Bridge
areas.text: The arched walkway from the gate across the water to the Armillary.

areas.name: The Star Arch
areas.text: The white arch with the gold star on top, the blue swirl filling it.

areas.name: The Watching Eyes
areas.text: The two gazers floating in the arch, one high and one low.

locations.name: The Sun Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A great gold archway in the dome's wall, crowned with a sun bigger than a house, and instead of a door there's a sheet of violet light with gold running through it like smoke, which is the only way in or out of the Seal. The golems built the wall around the whole place in arches so the sylphs could fly in and out, and the gate is the only part of it anything with feet can get through. Two golems stand in the gate and ask every comer one question, who they are, and they don't take a lie.

areas.name: The Gate Arch
areas.text: The gold arch itself, the sun over it, the violet light filling the doorway.

areas.name: The Gate Steps
areas.text: The paved road from the High Deck up to the arch, a gold ring set in the stones where you stop and answer.

areas.name: The Wall Walk
areas.text: The top of the arched wall either side of the gate, where the golems walk the round and the sylphs perch.

locations.name: The Sun Stair
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The long stair running from the Scales straight up the Seal's highest rock to the Needle, a white obelisk at the top with a gold sun ring standing behind it, and round shrines on the terraces either side all the way up. The souls the Scales weigh light go up this way, and on a quiet day you can see the air move on the steps as they pass. Nothing living climbs it. The golems stand at the bottom step and stop anyone trying, and they've never had to stop anyone twice.

areas.name: The Long Stair
areas.text: The straight white stair from the Scales to the summit, gold rails, the steps a little too tall for anything but golems.

areas.name: The Needle
areas.text: The white obelisk on the summit with the gold sun ring behind it, the top of the Seal.

areas.name: The Terrace Shrines
areas.text: The round domed shrines on the terraces either side of the stair, each one empty.

locations.name: The Swirl
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A hole in the floor of the Seal where the rock breaks open on a slow violet whirlpool with gold light spiralling into it and no bottom anybody has found. It's where the souls go, the ones the Scales have weighed, pulled round and round and down, and the wraiths are the ones that wouldn't go, hanging round the edge and grabbing at anything warm. A thin stone bridge crosses the top of it to a lone shrine on the far cliff, and the golems cross it twice a day for reasons they don't share.

areas.name: The Far Shrine
areas.text: The little round shrine on the cliff past the bridge, the only thing on that side.

areas.name: The Swirl Bridge
areas.text: The thin arched bridge over the whirlpool, gold rails, no wider than two people.

areas.name: The Wraith Rim
areas.text: The broken rock lip around the Swirl where the wraiths hang.

locations.name: The Turning Floor
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 22-24 · Danger: High]

The whole floor turns, slowly, a great wheel of stone grinding round under your feet, so the way you came in isn't where you left it. Stand still too long and the walls take your exit away.

areas.name: Fall Shaft
areas.text: A doorway the floor has turned away from, now opening onto a straight drop.

areas.name: Gear Gallery
areas.text: A gallery looking down through a crack onto great stone gears grinding in the dark.

areas.name: Still Point
areas.text: The middle of the turning floor, a small round stone that doesn't move while everything round it grinds past.

areas.name: Turning Hall
areas.text: A huge round hall whose floor moves in a slow circle, doorways passing like hours.

locations.name: The Two Gaps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

The road isn't one road, it's three stone decks with nothing between them but a ring of gold light turning over the drop, and you cross a gap by walking into the ring and trusting it. Most do, because the ones that turned back are still sitting on the landing. A gap carries anything that walks into it to the next deck, and the gargoyles on the deck posts watch every crossing and remember every face.

areas.name: The Gold Rings
areas.text: The two turning rings of light over the drop, humming low, loose stones floating round their edges.

areas.name: The High Deck
areas.text: The last deck, right up against the Sun Gate, with gargoyles on every post.

areas.name: The Low Deck
areas.text: The first stone deck past the landing, gold lines in the floor running straight at the first ring.

locations.name: The Undertow
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 36-38 · Danger: Severe]

The water on this floor pulls down. Not toward the sea, down, through holes in the floor toward the Heart, and anything that can't hold on goes with it. Iron rings are hammered into every wall.

areas.name: Grip Rings
areas.text: Walls studded with iron rings to hold on to, worn bright by hands and claws.

areas.name: Pull Hall
areas.text: A flooded hall where the water swirls toward holes in the floor.

areas.name: Snag Ledge
areas.text: A ledge above the pull where everything the water couldn't take down got caught, bones, packs and a few still breathing.

areas.name: Whirl Shaft
areas.text: A shaft where the water spirals straight down into the dark.

locations.name: The Vaults
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

Big square stone blocks on stepped terraces in the north of the prison, each one as big as a house with a gold line running round it and a gold ring on its side where the lock is, and stairs going up and down between them. Each one holds a prisoner, sealed in and left. The imps walk the terraces with their keys and stop at each block to listen. Some of them are quiet. Some of them knock back.

areas.name: The Listening Path
areas.text: The narrow path along the front of the blocks where the imps walk and listen.

areas.name: The Sealed Blocks
areas.text: The house-sized stone blocks, gold lines round each and a ring where the lock is.

areas.name: The Terrace Stairs
areas.text: The steps up and down between the terraces of blocks.

locations.name: The Violet Door
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 45-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A curved stone arch in the dome's wall where the road ends, filled with a sheet of violet light that moves like a whirlpool, the only door in the whole prison. An imp with a ring of keys longer than its arm sits on the step and asks what you've come for, and there are only two right answers, visiting or staying. Say anything else and the imp asks again with the hellhounds standing behind you.

areas.name: The East Wall
areas.text: The spiked violet wall either side of the door, a hellhound pacing on top of it.

areas.name: The Key Step
areas.text: The step in front of the door where the key imp sits with its book.

areas.name: The Violet Arch
areas.text: The curved arch with the whirlpool of violet light in it.

locations.name: The Watching Vault
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 17-19 · Danger: Moderate]

A tall vault where the gazers gather, dozens of them floating up near the roof, every eye on you from the moment you walk in. They don't attack straight away. They wait to see what you do, and they remember it.

areas.name: Blind Corridor
areas.text: A low passage the gazers can't see into, scratched with the marks of everyone who hid there.

areas.name: Blind Spot
areas.text: The one corner of the vault the gazers can't see into, small, crowded and full of everything that ever hid there.

areas.name: Eye Ceiling
areas.text: A vaulted roof crowded with floating gazers, their eyes glinting in the dark.

areas.name: Gazer Nest
areas.text: A crack in the wall full of small gazers, eyes not yet opened.

locations.name: The Waterhole
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 6-16 · Danger: Moderate]

The one deep pool for miles in the long grass, and by day everything drinks side by side under a truce nobody wrote down, then the sun goes and the gnolls come out of the grass to see who stayed too long.

areas.name: Pool Edge
areas.text: A muddy bank round a still brown pool, tracks of every size in the mud, tall grass all round.

locations.name: The Weeping Wall
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 38-40 · Danger: Severe]

The bottom of the water road, where the water stops being a flood and runs down one huge wall in sheets, salt crusting on everything and the air thin. Past it, the walls start to feel warm.

areas.name: Last Air
areas.text: A thin pocket of stale air at the bottom of the road, the last breath before the Heart.

areas.name: Salt Crust Hall
areas.text: A hall crusted thick with white salt crystals, crunching underfoot.

areas.name: Salt Pans
areas.text: Flat pans of white salt left by the water running down the wall, crusted thick, crunching under every step.

areas.name: Weeping Wall
areas.text: A wall as high as a cliff with water sheeting down it, salt white on every ledge.

locations.name: The Whispering Deep
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 46-48 · Danger: Deadly]

Every soul the dungeon has taken passes through here on its way to the Soul Well, and you hear them, all of them, whispering at once. An Aberrant hears its own kept souls answering.

areas.name: Memory Pool
areas.text: A pool that shows the last thing a soul saw if you lean over it.

areas.name: Old Voices
areas.text: A quiet room where only a few old voices speak, slow and clear.

areas.name: Quiet Hollow
areas.text: The one hollow in the deep where the voices stop, and the silence after them is worse.

areas.name: Whisper Halls
areas.text: Halls full of soft overlapping voices with nobody there.

locations.name: The Womb
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 43-45 · Danger: Deadly]

This is where the dungeon makes its monsters: walls bulging with shapes, things half-born pushing out of the stone. Every slime, mimic and keeper in the Great Dungeon started on this floor.

areas.name: Birthing Walls
areas.text: Walls swollen with shapes pressing out from inside, a claw or a face showing through.

areas.name: Cord Hall
areas.text: A hall strung with thick cords running from the walls down into the floor below.

areas.name: Failed Brood
areas.text: A chamber where the things the dungeon made wrong are left, too many legs or not enough, and most of them are still alive.

areas.name: Hatchling Floor
areas.text: A floor crawling with newly made monsters, small and wet and hungry.

locations.name: Tidepool Steps
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: Moderate]

Rock pools stepping down the cliff to the sea, full of crabs, weed and whatever the tide left behind, where anything hungry can eat its fill for free.

areas.name: Low Pool
areas.text: The bottom step of the pools, right at the water's edge, a deep round pool that never drains.

locations.name: Titan Bones
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-40 · Danger: Severe]

A valley full of the bones of beasts so big you walk under the ribs like a roof, and the beasts that killed them still come to eat what's left.

areas.name: Rib Road
areas.text: A path through the valley that runs under a ribcage as long as a town, moss growing on the bone.

locations.name: Toll Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A human toll gate on the old road east, the striped barrier still down across the road and the toll house beside it with the coins still in the box, and nothing has dared lift the bar.

areas.name: Barrier
areas.text: A wooden road barrier painted in faded stripes across an old stone road, a small toll house beside it.

locations.name: Turtle Back
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A green island with a spring, trees and a beach, good ground for anyone who wants their own place out on the sea. It moves a little every year, which the people who've lived on it say you stop noticing.

areas.name: Shell Shore
areas.text: A pale beach on a green island, the sand strangely ridged and warm underfoot.

locations.name: Vine Bridge
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 25-35 · Danger: Severe]

A bridge of living vines grown across a river gorge in the Deepgreen, thick as a troll's arm and bouncing under every step, the only crossing for a day either way.

areas.name: Vine Span
areas.text: The middle of the vine bridge, swaying and bouncing over the gorge, the river loud a long way below.

locations.name: Wall Fields
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-38 · Danger: Severe]

Overgrown human fields at the top of the falls with a broken stone wall round them, wheat gone wild and higher than a goblin, and the river running past on its way to the drop.

areas.name: Broken Wall
areas.text: A broken stone wall round fields of wild wheat, a river running past toward a cliff edge.

locations.name: Walled Farm
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-50 · Danger: Deadly]

A human farm inside a high wall with its fields still in rows and a gate that locks from the inside. It's still locked. Something inside has been keeping the rows weeded.

areas.name: Weeded Rows
areas.text: Neat rows in a walled field, not a weed in them.

locations.name: Watch Hill
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A bare hill with a stone watch post on top, looking west over the Iron March. Whoever holds it sees what's coming first.

areas.name: Watch Post
areas.text: A round stone post on the hilltop, a fire laid in an iron basket, the west wide open below.

locations.name: White Orchard
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

Rows of fruit trees on the hillside in white blossom all year round, even with snow on the ground round them, and the petals never seem to run out however hard the wind blows.

areas.name: Blossom Rows
areas.text: Rows of trees heavy with white blossom on a green slope, petals drifting over the snow at the edges.

locations.name: Windcut Pass
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 15-26 · Danger: High]

A narrow pass between two peaks of the Spine where the wind never stops and the cold will freeze a lizardfolk where it stands, the only way over the mountains that doesn't go through the hive.

areas.name: Pass Floor
areas.text: The floor of the pass between the peaks, packed snow and bare rock, the frozen travellers sat along both sides.

locations.name: Wormholes
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-20 · Danger: Moderate]

Rockworms have chewed this floor into holes, round tunnels going every way including straight up and down, and the walls hum when one's moving close. They don't hunt you. They just don't stop when you're in the way.

areas.name: Chewed Tunnels
areas.text: Perfectly round tunnels through solid rock, still warm from whatever bored them.

areas.name: Hum Chamber
areas.text: A round chamber where the worm tunnels meet and the walls hum loud enough to make your teeth ache.

areas.name: Ore Teeth
areas.text: A seam where the worms stopped, rock bitten in long curved grooves with iron glinting in them.

areas.name: Worm Cast Hall
areas.text: A hall heaped with grey worm casts, soft as ash, hiding bits of ore.

locations.name: Wreck Bay
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 12-22 · Danger: Moderate]

A bay full of wrecked ships on the rocks, good timber and iron for anyone who can strip them before the sea takes them.

areas.name: Wreck Line
areas.text: Broken hulls along the rocks, gulls on every mast, the tide sucking through the gaps.

locations.name: Wreckers' Light
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 20-30 · Danger: High]

A fire pit on a high black rock where the wreckers light a fire on stormy nights to bring the ships in wrong, onto the reef below, then row out in the morning to pick over what washed up.

areas.name: Fire Rock
areas.text: A blackened stone fire pit on top of a high sea rock, the reef and broken ship timbers far below.

locations.name: Wyrm Gate
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 30-45 · Danger: Deadly]

A ring of tall standing stones on a rise above Wyrm Ice, the stones carved with drakes eating their own tails. The drakes land here before they go into the ice and don't let anything else land with them.

areas.name: Landing Stones
areas.text: A circle of carved standing stones on a rise, the snow inside it scorched.

locations.name: Wyrm Ice
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 35-45 · Danger: Deadly]

Caves of blue ice where the frost drakes the ogres call wyrms sleep coiled in the cold, so still you can walk past one and think it's part of the wall.

areas.name: Ice Caves
areas.text: Blue tunnels of old ice, frost drakes coiled in the walls, breath freezing in the air.

locations.name: Wyvern Roost
locations.info:
[Recommended Level: 18-30 · Danger: High]

Cliffs high on the Spine covered in wyvern nests, bones scattered on every ledge, the sky over it never empty.

areas.name: Nest Ledges
areas.text: Cliff ledges thick with nests, bones and droppings, the wind howling up from below.

factions.name: The Big Table
factions.info: The bosses of Delvers' Rest, the ones strong enough to eat at the long table in the Big Hall. They keep the caravans running and the dungeon mouth open, settle fights before they wreck the town, and take a cut of everything.

factions.name: The Hive
factions.info: The antfolk of Hivehold, millions of them under one queen. They mine, build and trade iron and stone, and they deal with outsiders only on the guest ledge. They don't lie and they don't forget.

factions.name: The Horn Moot
factions.info: The herds of the long grass, centaurs, minotaurs and boarfolk, bound by the moot law: no blood spilled inside the ring of stones. They trade stock and hides, and they keep the grass road safe for anyone who keeps the law.

factions.name: The Laughing Pack
factions.info: A gnoll pack out of the Bonefield, laughing all night, raiding herds and caravans, and getting bigger every season. They answer to a witch and they take anyone who'll run with them.

factions.name: The Quiet Council
factions.info: The council of the dead that runs Stillbarrow: skeletons, ghouls and wraiths who have kept the same laws for three hundred years. They trade in bones, bodies and news, and they never forget a debt.

factions.name: The Red Fins
factions.info: Sharkfolk raiders on the Broken Coast who hit anything that floats and anything on the shore. They paint a red fin on everything they take, and they sell what they steal inland through anyone who'll buy.

creatures.name: Antfolk
creatures.info: That hill on the horizon isn't a hill, it's an antfolk mound, and if you get close enough you'll see the lines, thousands of them in perfect single file, carrying logs and stones ten times their size up the slope without ever once bumping into each other. They're many-legged hive people, soldiers and workers serving a queen nobody outside the mound ever sees, and they act like one body, so a lone antfolk is harmless and a hundred of them move, turn and strike together without a word passing between them. They talk by scent and trade worked earth and hard labour, and a town that hires a crew can have a wall up in a day, but a town that angers one finds the whole mound on its doorstep by morning.

creatures.name: Arachne
creatures.info: At dawn an arachne canyon looks like it's iced over, silk bridges and walkways strung wall to wall in their hundreds and every strand catching the light, and in the middle of it is a market selling the finest cloth anywhere in monster country. They're spider from the waist down and women from the waist up, and they run their silk cities like merchant houses, weaving, haggling and taking metal for cloth at prices that'd make a goblin weep. Along the edge of every market hangs a row of fat white cocoons, and if you ask, an arachne will tell you plainly that's the larder, and that most of what's in it was a customer who tried to leave without paying.

creatures.name: Basilisk
creatures.info: In the dungeon's middle depths you'll find the statues before you find the basilisk, adventurers and monsters in grey stone, mid-swing, mid-scream, mid-run, some of them so old they've worn smooth and some so fresh their packs are still full. A basilisk is a long eight-legged lizard with a hide like rough granite and dull yellow eyes, and one good look into those eyes greys you over from the skin inward. Everyone who's lived through meeting one says the same thing, watch its feet, never its face, because a basilisk doesn't talk, doesn't trade and doesn't need to chase you, it just needs you to look up.

creatures.name: Bearkin
creatures.info: In summer the northern rivers are full of bearkin, huge shaggy shapes standing knee-deep in the rapids scooping out salmon, and if you're polite they'll share a fire, a fish and a horn of honey-mead and rumble stories at you half the night. In winter they seal their caves and sleep, and the claw marks on the trees around a den, higher than any man could reach, are a warning to anyone thinking of waking one early. They're slow to anger and it takes a lot to get there, but a roused bearkin mauls whatever's in front of it until it stops moving, and the northern villages pay them in furs and honey to stand between them and everything else that comes down from the snow.

creatures.name: Boarfolk
creatures.info: Under the oaks where boarfolk live the forest floor is ploughed up like a field, dug over for acorns and roots, and every big trunk has its bark rubbed away at hip height where some bristle-backed brute has scraped its tusks sharp. They live in sounders led by the oldest sow, and that matriarch's word decides where the sounder roots and who it charges, which is usually anything that crosses its ground. Boarfolk speak bluntly and trade acorn-flour and hides, and they never back down, not from a bear, not from an orc warband and not from a fight they're obviously losing, so the smart move is not to start one with them at all.

creatures.name: Catfolk
creatures.info: The first catfolk most people see is sprawled across the warmest roof in a trade town, tail hanging over the edge, watching the street with half-shut eyes, and the second time they look up it's gone and so is somebody's coin. They're lithe and tufted and proud of it, hunters in the jungles and thieves and duellists in the towns, and they drop off rooftops and land on their feet without a sound. A catfolk will work for you, travel with you and even fight beside you, until something more interesting comes along and they're gone without a goodbye, and they collect curios the way other races collect grudges, odd trinkets they'll trade with you for a story worth hearing.

creatures.name: Centaur
creatures.info: On the grass seas you see a centaur herd long before you meet one, a line of dust along the horizon that never seems to get closer, and by the time you've counted them they've already ridden a full circle around you and decided whether you're a guest or a target. Horse below and person above, they live on the move in proud herds of archers and lancers who can put an arrow through a running hare at full gallop. Guests get fed, protected and sent off with a gift, but fences get torn down and burned wherever a herd finds them, because to a centaur a fence is someone claiming land that belongs to the wind, and the one who built it had better hope they aren't home.

creatures.name: Cockatrice
creatures.info: The ruined galleries where cockatrices nest are full of little statues, stone rats, stone birds, a stone goblin with one arm still flesh and a look on its face nobody likes to think about. A cockatrice has the head of a rooster, the body of a lizard and the temper of both, and its peck spreads stone through flesh like frost spreading over a puddle, slow enough that you get to watch it happen. They don't talk, they crow, at all hours and for no reason anyone can work out, and that crowing echoing down a gallery is the only warning you'll get to turn around and go back the way you came.

creatures.name: Crabfolk
creatures.info: Crabfolk villages are walled with shells, thousands of them stacked and cemented together along the tide-flats, and the houses inside are built sideways and low because that's how a crabfolk thinks about everything. They're broad and hard-shelled with one great crushing claw and one small clever one, and any ship that wrecks along their coast is picked clean by morning, timber, rope, cargo and all, because salvage is what the crabfolk live on. They're stubborn as the rock pools they guard, they clack when they talk and they trade salvage, and if you want to haggle with one you'd best be patient, a crabfolk will come at any deal from the side and never straight on.

creatures.name: Cyborg Cat
creatures.info: A cat with a cyborg body of black plates and orange-lit joints; Hawk is the only one anyone has met. He steps out of a portal ring, gives a party a boon for nothing and leaves; never hostile, never fights, wants nothing back, and treats every player as someone worth being generous to.

creatures.name: Drake
creatures.info: The rocks out in the volcanic badlands are scorched black in long fans where something has breathed fire across them, and if you follow the scorching back you'll find a drake asleep on a heap of bright metal it took off whoever came before you. They're horse-sized dragons with no wings and a lot of pride, they preen their scales, they sulk when they're ignored and they'll fight to the death over a shiny buckle. Most drakes never learn to talk, but the old ones do, and an elder drake will hear you out from on top of its hoard and let you pass if the tribute you brought is bright enough, and burn you where you stand if it isn't.

creatures.name: Dryad
creatures.info: In every old grove there's one tree greener and older than the rest, and if you look at its roots you'll see the axes, rusted and half-swallowed by the bark, from every logger who ever tried to cut it. That tree has a dryad in it, a woman of bark and leaf who can step out of the trunk as easily as through a doorway, and she'll sing intruders to sleep where they stand and wake the roots to wrap them up while they dream. They speak with the whole forest's voice, birds and branches and wind all at once, and the only thing a dryad will ever trade for is the grove's safety, everything else is just something walking on her floor.

creatures.name: Fox Spirit
creatures.info: There's a simple way to tell how much trouble a fox spirit is, count the tails, one is a clever animal, three is a trickster who can wear a face, and anything past five has been around long enough to own half the road and most of the people on it. They live on the edges of every town and crossroads, sometimes as a fox in the hedge and sometimes as the stranger at the inn whose shadow doesn't quite match, and they love a deal more than they love anything. A fox spirit speaks beautifully and trades in favours, and every word it says is true in a way, just never the way you took it, so by the time you work out what you actually agreed to it's already collecting.

creatures.name: Gargoyle
creatures.info: In the towns that pay gargoyles there's a stone figure perched on every rooftop, and if you pay attention you'll notice each one is crouched in a slightly different pose every morning than it was the night before. They're winged statues that wake when the sun goes down, guarding ruined spires and any town willing to show them the respect they ask for, and turning back into stone by day. A gargoyle talks in a grinding voice like millstones turning, and what it wants in trade is respect, a proper greeting, a share of the harvest set out on the roof, and a town that forgets its manners finds its guardians gone one morning and a lot of things it was being protected from coming in through the dark.

creatures.name: Gazer
creatures.info: Everyone who goes into the dungeon's deep halls gets the feeling they're being watched, and in a gazer's halls it's true, a floating eyeball the size of a barrel drifting just out of the torchlight with a ring of eyes on stalks around it, each one fixed on a different thing. Gazers are paranoid and clever and they always float with their back to a wall, and every stalk-eye casts its own curse, one to weaken, one to slow, one to burn, so a fight with one is a fight with a dozen spellcasters sharing one bad temper. They talk, and they'll trade what they know, which is a lot, for anything new to look at, a painting, a strange coin, a face they haven't seen before.

creatures.name: Ghoul
creatures.info: The graves in a ghoul-haunted cemetery are all dug up from the bottom, coffins split open from underneath and the dirt on top barely disturbed, and that's because ghouls tunnel in for their meals rather than dig down for them. They're grey, hunched corpse-eaters with long tongues and longer claws, and one scratch from a ghoul locks your muscles up stiff so it can feast on you at its leisure while you're still awake. Some of them still talk, and they'll trade grave-goods, rings, coins and old swords dug out of the coffins they emptied, to anyone who brings them a fresh body in return, no questions asked.

creatures.name: Gnoll
creatures.info: Out on the dry plains the laughing starts after dark, high cackles going back and forth across the grass, and anyone who's lived there long enough knows it means a gnoll pack has found something to run. They're stooped, spotted, hyena-headed things that don't fight their prey so much as follow it, for a day, for three, until it falls over from exhaustion and they eat it where it drops, still kicking. A caravan they've hit is easy to recognise, every bone cracked open for the marrow and every crate gone, and what they don't eat turns up later in their camps as trade, bones, teeth and other people's belongings, haggled over in barks and giggles that never quite stop.

creatures.name: Goblin
creatures.info: Goblins are small creatures but no less deadly. They live in groups and hunt in packs, and they use tricks and terrain to their advantage. While goblins have short lifespans they breed fast and in huge numbers, so there are always more of them. They live in hovels or caves in huge groups, keeping the weaker ones at the back with the children, usually a gaggle of morons or low intellects. Every once in a while a higher tier or station of goblin, a general, a king or a witch-hag shaman, will organise this gaggle of chaotic little biters into a dangerous and co-ordinated mass of teeth, claws and tools.

creatures.name: Golem
creatures.info: The dust on a golem's shoulders is a hand deep, because it's been standing in the same spot, in the same sealed vault, doing exactly the same job since long before anyone alive was born. They're bodies of clay, stone or iron with a rune cut into them somewhere that glows when they wake, and they follow the last orders their makers gave them right down to the letter, whether that still makes sense or not. Golems don't talk, but some of them will stop for a password, and treasure hunters spend years digging through ruins for the right words, because every vault guarded by a golem is a vault that's never been robbed.

creatures.name: Hamsterfolk
creatures.info: Hamsterfolk are stout, round beastfolk with stretchy cheeks who carry everything they own in their mouths and never give any of it back.

creatures.name: Harpy
creatures.info: You can spot a harpy cliff from miles off, the rock is streaked white from top to bottom and the ledges glitter with everything they've ever snatched, buckles, spoons, rings, a soldier's helmet, and the screeching coming off it never once lets up. They have women's faces on bird bodies, wings for arms and talons that can carry off a goat, and every colony is run by one old matriarch who decides who raids and who gets fed. Harpies trade feathers and stolen shinies happily enough, but cross one and she'll remember your face for the rest of her life, and travellers have been dropped on from the sky ten years after they forgot they'd ever made an enemy.

creatures.name: Hellhound
creatures.info: Down near the lower vents the tunnels smell of smoke and the floor is marked with scorched paw prints as wide as a dinner plate, and the baying that comes out of the dark sounds more like a forge's bellows than any dog. Hellhounds are black hounds the size of ponies with eyes like coals and jaws that smoke when they pant, and they run in packs that can follow a scent through ash and fire for days. They don't talk and they can't be tamed, only beaten, which is why a warlord with a hellhound at heel has already proved something to everyone watching, nothing breaks one to the leash but someone stronger than the whole pack.

creatures.name: Human
creatures.info: Humans built the town at the dungeon's mouth, you can still see it in everything, doors sized for something taller than a goblin and shorter than an ogre, writing carved over every archway that nobody left can read, rusted armour in the dungeon's upper halls shaped for bodies nobody here has. They were the adventurers, organised, armoured and always wanting something, land, cores, glory, and then the plague of men came and they died out or left, and the monsters came up out of the dungeon and moved into what was left. Their souls, the ones anyone has ever tasted, are strange and dense, packed with tools, language and memory, and most monsters in the Wildreach will tell you that humans are gone for good.

creatures.name: Hydra
creatures.info: Down where the dungeon floods, the hissing never comes from one place, it comes from five or six at once and it sounds like arguing, because it is, every head on a hydra has its own opinion and they bicker over every meal. It's a great swamp serpent with a body like a sunken boat and a tangle of necks, and cutting one off is the worst thing you can do, two more push out of the stump while you're still celebrating. The only adventurers who've ever killed one went in with torches and burned every neck shut the moment it was cut, and the ones who didn't know that are still down there in the black water, what's left of them.

creatures.name: Imp
creatures.info: Half the warlords in the Wildreach keep an imp around, a little horned, bat-winged thing perched on the back of a chair with a message scrawled on its arm in somebody else's handwriting, because nothing runs an errand faster through the dungeon than an imp. They're bred in the hot vents of the lower levels and they come up speaking every language there is, all of them badly, and they'll serve anyone who pays and sell that person out to the next one who pays more. You can always spot someone who stiffed an imp on the bill, they're the one with the itching rash, the bad luck and the boots that keep coming untied.

creatures.name: Kobold
creatures.info: Kobolds are knee-high to a man and they live like it, you'll find them in the old mines and the cracks between the stone, squeezing through gaps a cat would turn back from and nesting in shafts too narrow for anything bigger to follow. Most folk only know they're there from the sounds, claws ticking behind the rock, a yip in the dark, a pebble dropping where nobody's standing, and by the time you see the rust-red scales and the little dog snout it's usually because one of them wants you to. They never stop digging, every crack they move into gets wider, deeper and full of traps, so within a season an abandoned mine with kobolds in it is a maze of tripwires, pit drops and tunnels that loop back on themselves. They hoard anything that catches the light, chips of quartz, copper nails, a lost ring, and they pile the best of it in front of crude dragon shrines scratched into the walls, because every kobold believes the great wyrms are their kin and one day one will come down into the dark and claim them.

creatures.name: Lamia
creatures.info: Every oasis temple in the desert has a pool of clear water and a soft voice calling travellers to rest by it, and the sand around those temples is full of old bones that nobody ever talks about. A lamia is a woman from the waist up and a great scaled serpent from there down, and most people don't see the tail until she rises up out of the water and keeps rising. They speak sweetly and they trade in secrets and gold, and they're easy company for as long as you owe them nothing, but a lamia never forgets a debt, not a coin, not a favour and not an insult, and sooner or later every one of them gets collected in coils.

creatures.name: Lizardfolk
creatures.info: The log in the reeds blinks, that's usually the first and last thing anyone notices about a lizardfolk hunter, because they can lie in the marsh water so still and for so long that birds land on them. Their villages stand on stilts over the swamp, reed huts joined by rope bridges, nets drying on every rail, and nothing in them goes to waste, not fish bones, not shells, and not their own dead, who get eaten at the funeral by the family so the strength stays in the tribe. They're cold-eyed and patient and they don't care much about anything that isn't food, shelter or the next hatching, and they'll trade fish and shells with you in flat hisses without ever once looking like they wouldn't eat you too if the season was bad enough.

creatures.name: Mandrake
creatures.info: In old graveyards and the dungeon's gardens there's a plant with leaves that look a lot like a frown, and every gravedigger knows not to pull it, because under the dirt is a fat root with a face in it and the scream it lets out when it's yanked into the air drops everyone in earshot. Mandrakes are root-people, they pull themselves up and walk when they choose to, and they know every plant that grows, which ones heal and which ones kill. They don't talk much and they hate being dug up more than anything, but they'll trade herbs and poisons with anyone polite enough to knock on the soil first.

creatures.name: Mantid
creatures.info: You can walk straight past a mantid in the jungle, it's tall and green-plated and standing perfectly still among the leaves, and the first you know about it is the branch beside your head falling to the ground in two clean pieces. They live in hive monasteries in the deep jungle where every day is training, and a mantid can hold a single pose from dawn to dusk and then move faster than your eye can follow, those scythe forearms are folded one moment and through you the next. They click and chirr when they talk and they only trade with fighters they think are worth the time, which means that before you can buy anything off a mantid you'll have to show it what you can do.

creatures.name: Merfolk
creatures.info: On a still day you can look down through the water of the bay and see the drowned city, towers and streets far below with lights moving between them, and that's where the merfolk live, farming kelp in long green rows and fighting off whatever comes out of the deep with tridents. They're fish-tailed people with voices like music, and they trade pearls and coral with the coastal monster towns, but always from the water, they won't set foot on a dock or let anyone from the land into their city. Ask why and you'll get an old story about the land taking something from them a long time ago, told like it happened last week, because to the merfolk it might as well have.

creatures.name: Mimic
creatures.info: Every adventurer who lasted in the Great Dungeon learned the same lesson, the chest sitting alone in an empty room is too clean, too new and far too convenient, and the ones who didn't learn it fed a mimic. They're shapeshifters that wear the shape of chests, doors, treasure piles and loose flagstones, holding still for weeks until something reaches for the lid, and then the lid has teeth. The old ones are full of what they've eaten, rusted swords and coin purses rattling around in their guts, and a very old mimic can even talk, though they never trade, they've had everything they want handed to them for as long as anyone can remember.

creatures.name: Minotaur
creatures.info: Minotaur halls are built to lose people, corridors that fold back on themselves, doors that open onto walls, stairs to nowhere, and the stone floors are worn into deep grooves by hooves that have walked the same paths for generations. The minotaurs themselves never get lost, a bull-headed giant will walk you through its maze without a glance at the turns while you're still trying to remember which way was out. They're patient as herders until something sets them off, and the gouges in the walls at horn height show what happens then, a minotaur in a charge goes through doors, through shields and through whatever is holding them. They speak slow and plain and they trade bronze and hard labour, and a deal with one is good for exactly as long as you keep your end.

creatures.name: Mousefolk
creatures.info: Mousefolk are small, quick, big-eared beastfolk who get into every town because nobody notices them until they're already in.

creatures.name: Myconid
creatures.info: Deep in the dungeon's damp caves the walls start glowing a faint blue and the floor goes soft underfoot, and then you notice the rows, neat little farms of mushrooms tended by grey, cap-headed people who all turn to look at you at exactly the same moment. Myconids share their thoughts through spores, so what one of them sees the whole colony knows, and they're gentle folk who farm, heal and turn their dead into the compost that grows the next crop. Leave them be and they'll trade you mushrooms and medicine that'll cure nearly anything, but threaten the colony and the air fills with a cloud that leaves you dazed, sick or calm enough to sit there while they decide what to do with you.

creatures.name: Ogre
creatures.info: You can tell where an ogre's been by what's missing, the sheep from the paddock, the barrel from the cellar, the door off the cellar, and you can smell where it is long before you see it, a great slab of a thing twice a man's height with a gut like a rain barrel and hands that hang down past its knees. They have to stoop under every roof and turn sideways through every gate, so most of them don't bother and sleep out in the open on a pile of bones from everything they've eaten, which is anything, raw or rotten or still kicking. They aren't clever and they don't need to be, so every race in the Wildreach hires them as muscle and pays them in meat, and an ogre remembers every feast it was ever given and every meal anyone ever stole from it, feed one well and it'll walk through a wall for you, let its belly empty mid-job and it'll start eyeing the nearest thing that looks soft.

creatures.name: Orc
creatures.info: Big and warhungry brutes with muscle like iron and heads like steel, they live for war and fighting and think anyone who wants to waste time talking is weak and not worth their blood on an axe. Taller than most men, shorter than trolls but no less deadly, they raise warriors from birth to wield bigger and bigger weapons. The men and women fight equally, and some women are even deadlier than the men. They sport hulking frames and huge proportions, the females built like amazons, the men built like a steel wall with teeth. Their tribe means everything and their leader's words are absolute, until that leader starts to become weak or act in their own interests, then it's a challenge just waiting to happen.

creatures.name: Pixie
creatures.info: When the milk sours overnight, the horse's mane is knotted into a hundred tiny braids and your boots are full of beetles in the morning, there's a pixie meadow somewhere close. They're hand-sized, gossamer-winged little things that swarm the wildflowers in their hundreds, and everything they do is a joke, it's just that most of their jokes are cruel and some of them are deadly. The giggling always comes from somewhere just out of reach, and they trade in mischief and dreams, so a deal with one gets you a dream worth having and costs you something you won't notice is gone until much later.

creatures.name: Raccoonfolk
creatures.info: Raccoonfolk are small ringtailed tinkerers with clever hands and no sense of danger, who live off what everyone else throws away.

creatures.name: Ratfolk
creatures.info: Every monster town has ratfolk under it, and you'll find out the day your knife goes missing and turns up on a ratfolk stall two streets over before noon, with a hunched, whiskered little seller swearing it's been in the family for years. They live in the sewers and the refuse pits in numbers nobody has ever counted, grain sacks gnawed open in the night, rope chewed through, a purse cut and gone before you felt the tug, and they sell rumours as quickly as they sell stolen goods. A ratfolk will sell out their closest friend for a full belly and expect you to understand, and their bite carries every filthy thing they've ever crawled through, so the ones who fight them usually die of the fever a week later rather than the wound.

creatures.name: Rockworm
creatures.info: Maps of the dungeon go wrong every season and rockworms are why, one day there's a tunnel that wasn't there last time, perfectly round, smooth as glass and big enough to drive a cart through, and somewhere at the end of it something eyeless and as thick as a tree trunk is still chewing. You feel them before anything else, a low rumble under your boots that gets louder, and the smart thing is to get off the floor before the stone underneath you opens up and swallows you along with everything else in the way. They don't talk and they don't trade, but miners follow behind them anyway, because a rockworm's new tunnel is full of ore it didn't bother eating.

creatures.name: Salamander
creatures.info: The air shimmers in the dungeon's furnace halls and the stone floor glows where something has walked across it barefoot, and that's salamander country, red-scaled fire-lizards who lie in lava vents to rest and burn everything they touch. They're the best smiths anywhere near the Wildreach, a salamander doesn't need a forge, it picks up the iron in its own hands and works it hot, and the blades they trade come out sharper and harder than anything a hammer and coals can make. They talk in crackles and pops like a log on the fire, and they're friendly enough to anyone who brings them ore and doesn't mind singed eyebrows, but nobody shakes hands with one twice.

creatures.name: Satyr
creatures.info: You hear the pipes first, a tune drifting down out of the hill groves that gets into your feet before you've decided to listen, and the ones who follow it are found days later in some clearing, sore and wine-stained and danced half to death with no memory of how they got there. Satyrs are goat-legged, horned revellers who'll share their wine with anyone, and the same music that has a whole camp laughing can drop it asleep or send it running in a panic with a change of the tune. They speak sweetly, trade wine and songs and keep every promise they make until the sun comes up, and if you're angry about it they'll be sorry, honestly sorry, and play you something to help you forget.

creatures.name: Scorpid
creatures.info: The dunes rattle at dusk, a dry clicking that carries for miles across the sand, and caravan drivers who hear it double the watch and stop the camels, because it means scorpids are moving. They're armoured crawlers the size of a cart, claws that'll crush a man's leg, plates that turn a blade and a curled tail with a sting whose venom can stop a heart in a dozen beats. They raid the caravans, guard the ruins buried under the dunes and trade the salt and stolen goods they take, and you always know a camp has done business with them by the empty plates of chitin stacked by the tents, the old skins they shed and sold off as armour.

creatures.name: Shade
creatures.info: Your torch starts shrinking to an ember even though there's no wind, and the light ends a pace in front of you like it's hit a wall, and somewhere in that black is a shade. They're living darkness that pools in the dungeon's deepest places, and anything that walks into one goes cold and blind and finds the way out isn't where it was a second ago. Shades don't speak, but they can be bargained with if you sit in the dark long enough and ask quietly, and what they want in return is usually light, a lantern, a candle, a memory of the sun, which they swallow and keep forever.

creatures.name: Sharkfolk
creatures.info: Shore villages near sharkfolk waters build their watchtowers facing the sea instead of the land, because when a grey fin cuts across the bay at dusk a raid is coming before morning. Sharkfolk are grey-skinned reavers with rows of teeth behind rows of teeth, and they can smell one cut finger in the water from across the bay. Once blood starts flowing they frenzy, faster, harder and deaf to anything but the next bite, and even their own chiefs keep their distance until it passes. They snarl more than they speak and trade whatever they've plundered, and every coastal market has a stall of their loot, half of it still damp.

creatures.name: Siren
creatures.info: The reefs off the coast are piled with wrecks, ship on top of ship rotting on the rocks, and on calm nights the singing comes off them across the water, so sweet that sailors plug their ears with wax and tie themselves to the mast just to sail past. Sirens are feathered sea-singers who perch on the wreck-rocks and sing sailors right onto them, and then they drown the crew and pick through what's left of the cargo. They speak in song and trade pearls and drowned treasure, and every word out of a siren's mouth is the most beautiful lie you'll ever hear.

creatures.name: Skeleton
creatures.info: Walk through an old tomb and the bones are scattered all over the floor, walk back an hour later and every one of them is standing up again holding a rusted spear, and that's when you learn the bones down here don't stay down. Skeletons are held together by old magic and older orders, they guard tombs, they march in dead legions and they can be smashed apart a dozen times and still pull themselves back together, piece by rattling piece. They don't talk, they don't trade and they don't think for themselves, but now and then a necromancer speaks through one, and when a skeleton turns its head and says your name in somebody else's voice, whoever's on the other end already knows exactly where you are.

creatures.name: Slime
creatures.info: A dungeon corridor that's perfectly clean, no dust, no bones, not a dropped coin anywhere, means there's a slime living in it, because a slime eats everything it rolls over and leaves the stone behind spotless. It's a wobbling mass of acid jelly you can see straight through, and floating inside it you can usually spot whatever it ate last, a sword, a skull, half a goblin still dissolving. Young slimes don't think at all, they just eat, but the old ones have eaten enough minds to start one of their own, and they'll gurgle a deal at you and spit out polished treasure, cleaner than it's been in a hundred years, for something they haven't tasted yet.

creatures.name: Succubus
creatures.info: A succubus is a horned, bat-winged dungeon-born fiend who lives on charm and bargains and is a lot cleverer than she lets on.

creatures.name: Sylph
creatures.info: Up in the high passes the wind sometimes says your name, just once and quiet, and if you turn toward it you might catch the shape of someone in the blowing snow before it's gone. Sylphs are spirits of the wind with bodies you can only half see, and they ride the storms over the mountains for fun, stealing the breath out of travellers who aren't paying attention until they drop gasping in the drifts. They talk in whispers and trade in secrets, because the wind goes everywhere and hears everything, and a sylph who likes you can tell you what's being said about you three valleys over.

creatures.name: Treant
creatures.info: People who camp in the deep forest sometimes wake up and the path they walked in on isn't there any more, and the big oak that stood beside the fire last night is twenty paces to the left. That's treants, walking trees as old as the forest itself, so slow you'll swear they never move and so patient they can take a week to finish a sentence. They speak maybe once a season and only trade with someone willing to sit and wait for the answer, but anyone who brings an axe or a torch into their woods learns how fast a treant can be when it wants to, and what's left gets grown over by spring.

creatures.name: Troll
creatures.info: Trolls look like part of the riverbank until they move, long-armed and hunched with moss growing in the cracks of their hide and weed hanging off them from years spent sitting in the black water of the fens and under old bridges, waiting. You learn what they are the first time you cut one, the wound closes while you watch, and a lopped arm pushes a new one out of the stump by morning, so a troll fights without fear and without hurry and simply wears its prey down. The only scars they ever carry are burns, which is how everyone knows fire and acid are what they fear and why they stay in the wet and the dark. They love riddles more than gold, a troll will let a traveller pass for a good one and drown them for a bad one, and they trade only for things strange enough to be worth remembering, because when you live as long as a troll the only thing worth having is something new.

creatures.name: Vampire
creatures.info: Every village in the shadow of a vampire's castle looks the same, everyone pale and tired, shutters locked at sundown, and nobody will tell you why they keep wearing scarves in the heat. Vampires are pale, beautiful and very old, and they rule their courts from ruined castles like lords of the old kind, feeding on blood and charming the living into servants who'd happily die for them. They speak like nobles and trade in favours and blood-debts, and they're charming company for as long as you're useful, but they fear the sun more than anything, so whatever deal you make with a vampire, make it at noon.

creatures.name: Wolfkin
creatures.info: Wolfkin forests are marked, gouges dragged through the bark at the height of a tall man's head every few hundred paces, and if you keep walking past them the howls start, one ridge answering another until the whole valley knows where you are. They stand upright in grey and black pelts and live in packs bound by blood, and you can read a pack's whole order at a kill, the alpha eats first, the strong eat next and the young wait and watch and learn exactly where they stand. They'll trade furs and amber with you fair and square, but they never forget an insult, and a wolfkin who's been shamed will track the one who did it across half the Wildreach just to settle it.

creatures.name: Wraith
creatures.info: The candles gutter all at once, your breath fogs in the middle of summer and frost creeps across the walls in thin white fingers, and that's the only warning you get before a wraith comes through the stone. They're the cold shadows of souls that wouldn't move on, haunting battlefields and ruins and the dungeon's dark, and they drain the warmth out of anything living they touch until it's as cold as they are. Some still remember who they were and can be talked to, and they'll bargain hard for whatever it was that kept them here, a name, a grave, a debt nobody paid, but they never quite understand that the living can't wait forever for an answer.

creatures.name: Wyvern
creatures.info: Shepherds in the high country count their flock every evening, because a shadow passes over the hills now and then and afterwards there's one less sheep and nobody saw it go. Wyverns are two-legged, bat-winged lesser dragons that nest on the highest peaks in nests built from the bones of everything they've carried up, and they hunt by folding their wings and dropping out of the clouds onto whatever looks slow. The barbed sting on the end of their tail carries a venom that locks up the limbs, so whatever they don't kill in the dive just lies there waiting, and nobody bargains with a wyvern, it looks at you and sees dinner.

items.name: Biter's Collar
items.info: A collar of bone beads.

items.name: Biter's Hook
items.info: A gutting hook worn on the belt.

items.name: Calling Bones
items.info: A bag of carved knuckle bones for throwing.

items.name: Chief's Mantle
items.info: A hide mantle painted with every herd's colours.

items.name: Clerk's Ledger
items.info: A small ledger bound in grey leather, for writing down debts.

items.name: Copper Ore
items.info: A sack of green-streaked copper ore, ready for a smelter. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Rattle Warren's Junk Market.

items.name: Council Lamp
items.info: A lamp that burns cold and blue, and never goes out.

items.name: Councillor's Skull
items.info: A polished skull on a chain, worn by the council's own.

items.name: Crypt Key
items.info: An iron key that fits every crypt door in Stillbarrow.

items.name: Cut Stone
items.info: Squared blocks of grey chapel stone, ready for a wall. 2 Iron Ingot, sold at Stillbarrow's Bone Market.

items.name: Enforcer's Club
items.info: A heavy iron-shod club with the Table's mark burnt into the grip.

items.name: Fen Salve
items.info: A pot of green-black salve from the fen that stops bleeding and smells awful. 2 Iron Ingot, sold at Stiltscale's Stilt Market.

items.name: Fin Paint
items.info: A pot of red paint for marking what's been taken.

items.name: Finger Bone
items.info: A clean finger bone strung on a cord, the mark of a grave-hand.

items.name: Glow Moss
items.info: A sack of the dungeon's glowing moss, cut from warm stone. It lights a room for a week and heals small wounds packed into them. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Delvers' Rest's Swap Ground.

items.name: Grass Braid
items.info: A braid of long grass and horsehair given to runners of the moot.

items.name: Guest Chit
items.info: A chip of polished black stone; the guest ledge lets its bearer in.

items.name: Hand's Ring
items.info: An iron ring stamped with the Big Hall's roof.

items.name: Hardwood
items.info: A bundle of dense oak wood the old oak let fall on its own. Nothing in the Deep Wood is cut. 2 Iron Ingot, sold at Ringgrove's Root Steps.

items.name: Hauler's Strap
items.info: A woven strap for hauling, worn shiny by work.

items.name: Herd Bell
items.info: A bronze bell that every herd knows the sound of.

items.name: Hill Flint
items.info: A sack of flint from the watch hill, for fire-starting and for edges. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Delvers' Rest's Caravan Yard.

items.name: Horn Ring
items.info: A ring cut from horn, polished by the horn stone.

items.name: Human Flour
items.info: Sacks of fine white flour off a human mill wheel, the kind no monster town can grind. 2 Iron Ingot, sold at Delvers' Rest's Swap Ground.

items.name: Hydra Scale
items.info: A crate of shed hydra scales, hard as iron and light as bark, good for armour. 4 Iron Ingot, sold at Stiltscale's Stilt Market.

items.name: Iron Ingot
items.info: A palm-sized bar of smelted iron, the one measure every monster town agrees on. Trade is barter first; ingots settle what goods cannot.

items.name: Iron Ore
items.info: A sack of red-black iron ore; smelt enough of it and you have ingots. 2 Iron Ingot, sold at Hivehold's Guest Ledge.

items.name: Jungle Timber
items.info: Hard red jungle wood from the Deepgreen, heavy as stone and twice as easy to work. 3 Iron Ingot, sold at Stillbarrow's Bone Market.

items.name: Peat Bricks
items.info: A stack of cut and dried peat that burns slow and hot. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Stiltscale's Stilt Market.

items.name: Queen's Scent
items.info: A sealed vial of the queen's scent; antfolk smell it and step aside.

items.name: Red Fin Flag
items.info: A torn sail with the red fin painted on it.

items.name: Red Tooth
items.info: A shark's tooth painted red at the root.

items.name: Rock Salt
items.info: A block of white salt cut from the lick. Every herd wants it and every cook needs it. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Hornmoot's Herd Pens.

items.name: Runner's Cord
items.info: A knotted cord worn on the arm; every caravan master knows what it means.

items.name: Runner's Hide
items.info: A scrap of spotted hide worn as a sash.

items.name: Sand Glass
items.info: Plates of green glass cut from the flats. It hums faintly at night. 3 Iron Ingot, sold at Cinderforge's Glass Market.

items.name: Seat Token
items.info: A carved stone that matches the back of a chair at the long table.

items.name: Ship Timber
items.info: Salvaged hull planks and spars, salt-hard and still good. 2 Iron Ingot, sold at Saltreef's Tide Market.

items.name: Smoked Haunch
items.info: A whole smoked haunch of something big, enough to feed one hungry monster for a day. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Delvers' Rest's Big Hall.

items.name: Spring Salts
items.info: A crust of white salts scraped from the Rimelands' hot springs. Rubbed into a wound it stops the cold getting in. 3 Iron Ingot, sold at Hivehold's Guest Ledge.

items.name: Table Scrap
items.info: A bone chip off the long table, given to anyone who runs errands for the bosses.

items.name: Tide Boss Chain
items.info: A chain of stolen rings worn round the neck.

items.name: Toll Scrap
items.info: A sack of whatever travellers paid to cross a ford: buckles, knives, teeth, odd coins nobody uses any more. 1 Iron Ingot, sold at Rattle Warren's Junk Market.

items.name: Tooth Charm
items.info: A string of teeth, given to anyone who runs with the pack.

items.name: Tunnel Lamp
items.info: A lamp full of glowing beetles that never needs oil.

items.name: Turtle Pearls
items.info: Pearls the size of a thumb found in the warm sand of Turtle Back. Nobody asks where the sand gets them. 3 Iron Ingot, sold at Saltreef's Tide Market.

items.name: Warden's Mandible
items.info: A carved mandible worn at the throat.

items.name: Warden's Staff
items.info: A heavy staff topped with a ram's horn.

items.name: Witch's Mark
items.info: A smear of red ochre on the face that never washes off.

abilities.name: A Bit Wrong
abilities.info:
What it does: something you said earlier turns out true; you name one small detail of the place around you and it's that way now.

You mention, very casually, that the bridge was always rotten, or the door was always locked, or the guard was always asleep at this hour, and when they check, it is, and always was, and the whole countryside shifts a little to make room for it.
[Trait: Fox Liar-King]

abilities.name: A Million Would Die
abilities.info:
What it does: your hive throws itself in front of you; for a few turns any blow aimed at you is taken by a hive soldier instead.

They swing at you and a soldier throws itself in the way, and the next one, and the next, every one of them dying for you without a pause or a thought, a wall of loyal bodies between you and anything that wants you.
[Trait: Antfolk Queen]

abilities.name: A Year Gone
abilities.info:
What it does: one creature you put to sleep wakes believing much longer has passed than really has; they're lost and confused for a long time.

You stroke their hair while they sleep and whisper to them about the seasons going by, spring, summer, autumn, winter, and when they wake they're sure a whole year's gone, and they stagger out of the grove looking for a world that isn't there any more.
[Trait: Dryad Dreamweaver]

abilities.name: A Year in the Shallows
abilities.info:
What it does: you settle into the shallows and the reef on your back heals you; resting in water heals you fully.

You settle down into the shallows and go still and the fish come out of your coral to feed and the water washes over you, and the reef on your back grows over every crack and wound, and when you stand up again you're whole.
[Trait: Living Reef Crab]

abilities.name: Absorbed Memory
abilities.info:
What it does: you recall what you have digested; you know things that creatures you ate knew.

Your glowing core flickers and pulses and inside it something stirs, the last memories of everything you ever swallowed bubbling up through you, a goblin's warren paths, a merchant's hidden purse, a guard's patrol, and you know them now as well as they ever did.
[Trait: Elder Slime]

abilities.name: Abyss Sight
abilities.info:
What it does: you see perfectly in black water and darkness.

You sink down past where the light ends, the water going green, then blue, then black, and your lantern eyes open wide and glow, and the darkness opens up for you, every rock, every drifting jelly, every hidden thing in the deep lit up pale and clear.
[Trait: Deep Merfolk]

abilities.name: Abyssal Step
abilities.info:
What it does: you step from shadow to shadow across a whole field, striking a foe at every step.

You sink into one shadow and come out of another a hundred paces away, and strike, and sink again, and come out behind someone else, and strike, again and again from one end of the fight to the other, a cold black shape flickering from shadow to shadow faster than anyone can follow, leaving bodies in every patch of shade.
[Trait: Abyss Shade]

abilities.name: Acid Flood
abilities.info:
What it does: a wave of acid pours out over a wide area: every foe in it takes heavy acid damage and their armour and hide are ruined.
You throw your arms wide and it comes out of you in a wave, a flood of acid rushing out across the ground in every direction, over feet, over legs, over anyone who's fallen, and everything it touches smokes and melts and runs.
How it looks is theirs: narrate it the way they have said their element shows (their backstory, or what they said in play), and only fall back on this when they haven't.
[Trait: Acid: Acid Flood]

abilities.name: Acid Hide
abilities.info:
What it does: your hide oozes acid; anyone who strikes or grabs you is badly burned for a few turns as it eats into them.

Your skin goes slick and yellow-green and drips, hissing where it spatters the stone, and the fool who grabs you sinks in to the wrist, the skin on their fingers already bubbling, and when they tear free the skin of both hands stays behind on you, and they stand there staring at their own raw red fingers while the stink of boiled meat comes up off them.
[Trait: Ooze Troll]

abilities.name: Acid Pool
abilities.info:
What it does: spill a pool of acid on the ground for three turns: foes who stand in it or cross it take acid damage each turn.
You open your hand and it pours out, far more than your hand could hold, spreading across the ground hissing and smoking, and anything that steps in it hops and shrieks and stumbles straight into more.
How it looks is theirs: narrate it the way they have said their element shows (their backstory, or what they said in play), and only fall back on this when they haven't.
[Trait: Acid: Acid Pool]

abilities.name: Acid Rain
abilities.info:
What it does: acid falls on the area round you for two turns; every foe in it takes acid damage each turn and loses armour.
You throw your head back and spit up into the air and it comes back down as rain, a fine drizzle that sizzles on everything it touches, they throw their arms over their heads and their hair comes out in their hands, the stink of burning hide is everywhere, and there's nowhere to run because it's falling on all of them at once.
How it looks is theirs: narrate it the way they have said their element shows (their backstory, or what they said in play), and only fall back on this when they haven't.
[Trait: Acid: Acid Rain]

abilities.name: Acid Spit
abilities.info:
What it does: spit acid at one foe at range: acid damage, and it keeps burning for a turn.
You hawk it up and spit it, and it hits them with a hiss and starts smoking right away, and they're slapping at it and screaming as it eats in.
How it looks is theirs: narrate it the way they have said their element shows (their backstory, or what they said in play), and only fall back on this when they haven't.
[Trait: Acid: Acid Spit]

abilities.name: Acid Splash
abilities.info:
What it does: you splash burning acid on one foe or a few close together; they're burned and their gear is damaged.

You wobble up into a tall green blob and then slap down hard, and a wave of yourself splashes out over them, and wherever you hit it hisses and smokes, clothes melting, skin blistering red, and they're howling and tearing off their burning gear while you slide back together laughing in bubbles.
[Trait: Acid Slime]

abilities.name: Acid Touch
abilities.info:
What it does: your touch eats through cloth, leather, rope and wood like it's paper; living flesh it touches is burned.

You press yourself against it and it fizzes, a little hiss and a sour sharp smell, the leather going dark and soft and then just running, the rope parting strand by strand, and if it's a hand you've got hold of they rip it away from you shrieking with the skin of their palm left behind on you.
[Trait: Soul Gift: Acid Touch]

abilities.name: Across the Still Sea
abilities.info:
What it does: your song carries for miles; you send a message, a lure or a warning to anyone near any water you can see.

You sing out over the still water at night and the song goes, and goes, across the whole sea, low and clear, and far away on some other shore someone sitting by the water hears every word of it as if you were standing right behind them.
[Trait: Siren Reef-Queen]

abilities.name: All-Seeing
abilities.info:
What it does: you see in every direction at once; nothing can surprise you and you notice everything in sight.

Your stalks spread out around you, every one pointing a different way, and you see all of it at once, the door behind you, the ceiling above, the shadow creeping along the wall to your left, and when they try to sneak up on you there's already an eye looking straight at them.
[Trait: Gazer Watcher]

abilities.name: Alpha Stare
abilities.info:
What it does: you stare down the foes in front of you; the weaker ones back off, freeze or drop their guard, breaking their line.

You don't growl and you don't raise a weapon, you just go still, ears forward, lip lifting a little off your teeth, and you look at them, and something old in the back of their skulls remembers what the forest was like before fire, so the timid drop their eyes, then their weapons, and one or two go down on their backs in the dirt with their throats bared before they even know why.
[Trait: Wolfkin Alpha]

abilities.name: Always a Line
abilities.info:
What it does: you treat a whole group of the sick or wounded at once; each of them is healed and cured of sickness.

They're lined up at your patch of earth as always, and you work down the line without stopping, a leaf for this one, a root for that one, a word, a poultice, a hand on the brow, and by the end of the day every one of them walks away on their own feet.
[Trait: Mandrake Elder-Healer]

abilities.name: Always Thirsty
abilities.info:
What it does: every hit you land drinks a little blood; for the rest of the fight you heal a little from every hit.

You slosh forward and every time your claws or teeth go in you drink, you can't help it, a little mouthful every hit, and it goes down warm and fills you up and closes whatever they've done to you.
[Trait: Blood Fiend]

abilities.name: Ambush
abilities.info:
What it does: attack a foe who doesn't know you're there: the first hit lands with far more force.

You've been there for a while, close, watching it, waiting for it to turn its back, and when it does you come out of the dark and hit it before it ever knew there was a dark to come out of.
[Trait: Trained Stalk II]

abilities.name: Ambush Order
abilities.info:
What it does: you set your hunters in hiding; when the foe walks in the ambush springs all at once and every hunter's first strike lands hard.

You flick your tongue twice and the hunters melt into whatever cover there is, under the water, in the reeds, flat in the mud, and then there's nothing but frogs and the buzz of flies as the enemy comes splashing through, and you wait, and wait, until the last of them is in the middle of the trap, and then you hiss once and the cover all around them stands up with weapons in its hands.
[Trait: Lizardfolk Chieftain]

abilities.name: Ambush Web
abilities.info:
What it does: you trap one foe in a web and strike while they're stuck; they're held and your strike lands hard.

You flick a sticky line at their legs from the dark and they go down tangled, and before they can tear it loose you're scuttling at them on all eight legs, a horrible clicking rush, and you're on top of them, pinning them to their own web while your fangs sink in.
[Trait: Arachne Stalker]

abilities.name: Ancestor Fury
abilities.info:
What it does: you call the ancestors' fury down on your foes; spirit warriors strike at every enemy near you for a turn.

The bone charms on your staff howl with the voices of the dead, and you slam the end of it into the ground and roar the war-names of the tribe's oldest dead, and they come, grey and furious and bellowing war-names out of the earth, a charge of ghost-warriors with ghostly weapons swinging, and they cut through your foes and leave them bleeding and shaking before sinking back into the ground.
[Trait: Spirit Caller]

abilities.name: Ancestor's Counsel
abilities.info:
What it does: you ask the ancestor ghosts a question; they answer with what they knew in life, about a place, a foe or a choice ahead.

You close your eyes and the swirling smoke around you thickens into faces, old ones, scarred ones, and you ask, and they whisper back, all of them at once, and in the middle of the noise there's the answer, plain, from someone who learned it the hard way a long time ago.
[Trait: Spirit King]

abilities.name: Ancient Knowledge
abilities.info:
What it does: recall lost knowledge about a ruin, a relic or an old power: how it works, what it does, what it costs.

It comes up out of somewhere deep in you, an old song, a half-remembered drawing, a warning scratched on a wall a long way down, and you suddenly know what this thing does and why nobody should ever touch the red one.
[Trait: Trained Lore V]

abilities.name: Antfolk Swarm
abilities.info:
Coordinate allies to strike together.
[Trait: Soul of the Antfolk]

abilities.name: Apex
abilities.info:
What it does: for the rest of the fight you are the hunter here: every foe fears you, your hits land harder, and any that flee you catch.

Something in the air changes and every creature in the fight feels it at once, the old feeling at the back of the skull that says something bigger is here and it's hungry, and they all stop looking at each other and start looking at you.
[Trait: Trained Hunt VIII]

abilities.name: Arachne Web
abilities.info:
Cast a web to pin a foe or bridge a gap.
[Trait: Soul of the Arachne]

abilities.name: Army of One Mind
abilities.info:
What it does: for a few turns your allies move as one: each of them acts with you, covers the others and never misses an opening.

They stop being a crowd of separate fighters, every one of them moves when you move, covers when you cover, strikes when you strike, a single body with a hundred arms and your mind behind all of them.
[Trait: Trained Command VIII]

abilities.name: Army That Never Fought
abilities.info:
What it does: you wake your stone army for a while; the statues of those you've petrified fight for you for a few turns.

You look down at the field of statues and blink, slowly, and the stone army below you creaks and cracks and moves, every frozen soldier lurching forward stiff and grey to finally fight the battle they never got to.
[Trait: Stone Medusa Gargoyle]

abilities.name: Ask the Drowned
abilities.info:
What it does: you ask the swamp's dead what they saw; they answer with what happened in or near the water.

You crouch at the edge of the still black water with ghost-lights bobbing round your head and drop a fish bone into it and wait, and the bubbles come up, slow at first, then faster, and with each one that bursts a voice whispers out of it, wet and cold and old, telling you who came through here, what they carried, and where they went to die.
[Trait: Lizardfolk Spirit-Talker]

abilities.name: Ask the Echoes
abilities.info:
What it does: you ask a kept soul what it knew, a place, a face, a trick of its race; it answers, though not always kindly or truthfully.

You hold still and they rise up out of the dark inside you, a mutter, then a voice, then a crowd of them talking over each other, until one pushes to the front and tells you what it saw, the hidden turning, the face at the fire, the trick its kind used, then it laughs and sinks back down before you can ask if it was true.
[Trait: Echo-Bound]

abilities.name: Ask the Stars
abilities.info:
What it does: on a clear night you read the stars; you learn one thing about the days ahead, a danger, a path or a choice that matters.

You lie back in the grass and watch the stars lean down to listen to you, and you ask them, and they shift ever so slightly, a line here, a shape there, and you read the answer written up there across the whole sky.
[Trait: Centaur Astromancer]

abilities.name: At the Family Table
abilities.info:
What it does: wearing the shape of someone you ate, you fool those who knew them completely; they tell you anything.
